bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起玄黓涒灘，盡玄黓敦牂，凡十一年。

translations.literal: From Xuanyi Tuantan through Xuanyi Dunyang; eleven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Xuanyi Tuantan through Xuanyi Dunyang—eleven years in all.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，上行幸雍，祠五畤；

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars;

sentences.zh: 還，祝祠泰一，以拜德星。

translations.literal: on returning, he prayed and sacrificed to the Grand Unity, thereby paying homage to the Virtue Star.
translations.idiomatic: on his return he prayed and sacrificed to the Grand Unity to pay homage to the Virtue Star.

sentences.zh: ----2春，正月，公孫卿言：「見神人東萊山，若-{云}-欲見天子。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the first month, Gongsun Qing said: "I saw a spirit-man on Mount Donglai who seemed -{云}- to wish to see the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the first month, Gongsun Qing said, "I saw a spirit-man on Mount Donglai who seemed about to wish to see the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」天子於是幸緱氏城，拜卿為中大夫，遂至東萊，宿留之，數日，無所見，見大人跡-{云}-。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven thereupon favored Gou'shi city, appointed Qing as Palace Grandee, and proceeded to Donglai, lodging there several days without seeing anything—only the footprints of a great man -{云}-.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon visited Gou'shi, appointed Qing Palace Grandee, and went on to Donglai, where he lodged several days without seeing anything—only the footprints of a great man -{云}-.

sentences.zh: 復遣方士求神怪，采芝藥，以千數。

translations.literal: He again dispatched masters of the methods to seek spirits and marvels and gather mushroom elixirs, numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He again dispatched masters of the methods to seek spirits and marvels and gather mushroom elixirs, numbering in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 時歲旱，天子既出無名，乃禱萬里沙。

translations.literal: At that time the year was drought-stricken; the Son of Heaven having gone forth without a stated purpose, he thereupon prayed at Wanli Sands.
translations.idiomatic: The year was drought-stricken; the emperor having set out without a stated purpose, prayed at Wanli Sands.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，還，過祠泰山。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on returning he passed and sacrificed at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on his return he sacrificed at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: ----3初，河決瓠子，後二十餘歲不復塞，梁、楚之地尤被其害。

translations.literal: ----3 At the outset, the Yellow River burst at Huzi; for more than twenty years afterward it was not blocked again, and the lands of Liang and Chu were especially afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 At the outset the Yellow River burst at Huzi; for more than twenty years it was not blocked again, and Liang and Chu suffered worst.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上使汲仁、郭昌二卿發卒數萬人塞瓠子河決。

translations.literal: That year, the emperor sent the two ministers Ji Ren and Guo Chang to raise several tens of thousands of conscripts to block the Huzi breach.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor sent Ministers Ji Ren and Guo Chang to raise tens of thousands of conscripts to block the Huzi breach.

sentences.zh: 天子自泰山還，自臨決河，沈白馬、玉璧於河，令群臣、從官自將軍以下皆負薪，卒填決河。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, returning from Mount Tai, personally came to the breach, sank a white horse and jade disks in the river, and ordered the host of ministers and attendant officials from the generals down to all carry firewood—the soldiers filled the breach.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Mount Tai, the emperor came in person to the breach, sank a white horse and jade disks in the river, and ordered every minister and attendant from the generals down to carry firewood until the soldiers had filled the breach.

sentences.zh: 築宮其上，名曰宣防宮。

translations.literal: He built a palace upon it, named Xuanfang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He built a palace upon it and named it Xuanfang Palace.

sentences.zh: 導河北行二渠，復禹舊跡，而梁、楚之地復寧，無水災。

translations.literal: He guided the Yellow River north to run in two channels, restoring Yu's old course, and the lands of Liang and Chu were again at peace, without flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He guided the Yellow River north into two channels, restoring Yu's old course, and Liang and Chu were at peace again, without flood disaster.

sentences.zh: ----4上還長安。

translations.literal: ----4 The emperor returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 The emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: ----5初令越巫祠上帝、百鬼，而用雞卜。

translations.literal: ----5 For the first time he ordered Yue shamans to sacrifice to the High God and the hundred ghosts, and used chicken divination.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 For the first time he ordered Yue shamans to sacrifice to the High God and the hundred ghosts, and used chicken divination.

sentences.zh: ----6公孫卿言仙人好樓居，於是上令長安作蜚廉、桂觀，甘泉作益壽、延壽觀，使卿持節設具而候神人。

translations.literal: ----6 Gongsun Qing said that immortals love to dwell in towers; thereupon the emperor ordered Feilian and Gui Terrace built in Chang'an, and Yishou and Yanshou terraces built at Ganquan, and sent Qing with credentials to set out offerings and await the spirit-man.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Gongsun Qing said immortals love tower dwellings; the emperor ordered Feilian and Gui Terrace built in Chang'an and Yishou and Yanshou terraces at Ganquan, and sent Qing with credentials to set out offerings and await the spirit-man.

sentences.zh: 又作通天莖台，置祠具其下。

translations.literal: He also built the Tongtian Stem Terrace and placed sacrificial implements below it.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the Tongtian Stem Terrace and placed sacrificial implements below it.

sentences.zh: 更置甘泉前殿，益廣諸宮室。

translations.literal: He further established the front hall at Ganquan and greatly expanded the palaces and halls.
translations.idiomatic: He further established the front hall at Ganquan and greatly expanded the palaces and halls.

sentences.zh: ----7初，全燕之世，嘗略屬真番、朝鮮，為置吏，築障塞。

translations.literal: ----7 At the outset, in the age of united Yan, Yan had once roughly subordinated Zhenfan and Joseon, set officials over them, and built barrier fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 At the outset, in the age of united Yan, Yan had once subordinated Zhenfan and Joseon, appointed officials, and built barrier fortifications.

sentences.zh: 秦滅燕，屬遼東外徼。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Yan, they belonged to the outer marches of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin destroyed Yan, they fell within the outer marches of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 漢興，為其遠難守，復修遼東故塞，至浿水為界，屬燕。

translations.literal: When Han rose, because the region was remote and hard to hold, it restored the old Liaodong barriers, taking the Yalu River as the border, and they belonged to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose, finding the region remote and hard to hold, it restored the old Liaodong barriers with the Yalu River as border, and they belonged to Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕王盧綰反，入匈奴。

translations.literal: King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled and entered the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: King Lu Wan of Yan rebelled and fled to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 燕人衛滿亡命，聚黨千餘人，椎髻、蠻夷服而東走出塞，渡浿水，居秦故空地上下障，稍役屬真番、朝鮮蠻夷及燕亡命者，王之，都王險。

translations.literal: The Yan man Wei Man, a fugitive, gathered a party of more than a thousand men, wore topknots and barbarian dress, fled east out of the passes, crossed the Yalu, dwelt in Qin's old vacant lands between the upper and lower barriers, gradually subjugated the barbarians of Zhenfan and Joseon and Yan fugitives, made himself king, and established his capital at Wangxian.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan man Wei Man, a fugitive, gathered more than a thousand followers, wore topknots and barbarian dress, fled east beyond the passes, crossed the Yalu, settled in Qin's old vacant lands between the upper and lower barriers, gradually brought the barbarians of Zhenfan and Joseon and Yan fugitives under his rule, made himself king, and established his capital at Wangxian.

sentences.zh: 會孝惠、高-{后}-時，天下初定，遼東太守即約：滿為外臣，保塞外蠻夷，無使盜邊；

translations.literal: It happened that in the time of Emperor Hui and Empress Gao -{后}-, when all under Heaven was newly settled, the Governor of Liaodong at once made a pact: Man was to be an outer minister, guarding the barbarians beyond the passes and not letting them raid the border;
translations.idiomatic: It happened that in the time of Emperor Hui and Empress Gao -{后}-, when the realm was newly settled, the Governor of Liaodong at once made a pact: Man was to be an outer minister, guarding the barbarians beyond the passes and keeping them from raiding the border;

sentences.zh: 諸蠻夷君欲入見天子，勿得禁止。

translations.literal: if the chieftains of the various barbarians wished to enter and see the Son of Heaven, he was not to forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: if barbarian chieftains wished to enter and see the Son of Heaven, he was not to forbid them.

sentences.zh: 以故滿得以兵威財物侵降其旁小邑，真番、臨屯皆來服屬，方數千里。

translations.literal: For this reason Man was able with military might and wealth to invade and reduce the small settlements beside him; Zhenfan and Lintun all came to submit and belong to him—several thousand li square.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Man was able with military might and wealth to subdue neighboring settlements; Zhenfan and Lintun all submitted to him—several thousand li square.

sentences.zh: 傳子至孫右渠，所誘漢亡人滋多，又未嘗入見，辰國欲上書見天子，又雍閼不通。

translations.literal: The line passed from son to grandson Youqu; the Han fugitives he enticed grew ever more numerous, and he had never entered to pay court; the state of Chen wished to submit a memorial and see the Son of Heaven, but was again blocked and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed from son to grandson Youqu; the Han fugitives he enticed grew ever more numerous, and he had never come to court; the state of Chen wished to memorialize and see the Son of Heaven, but was blocked and obstructed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢使涉何誘諭，右渠終不肯奉詔。

translations.literal: That year, Han sent She He to entice and instruct him, but Youqu in the end refused to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: That year Han sent She He to entice and instruct him, but Youqu refused to obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 何去至界上，臨浿水，使御刺殺送何者朝鮮裨王長，即渡，馳入塞，遂歸報天子曰：「殺朝鮮將。

translations.literal: When He reached the border, facing the Yalu, he had his charioteer stab and kill Chang, the Joseon assistant king who was escorting him, then immediately crossed, galloped into the passes, and returned to report to the Son of Heaven: "I killed a Joseon general.
translations.idiomatic: When He reached the border at the Yalu, he had his charioteer stab and kill Chang, the Joseon assistant king escorting him, crossed at once, galloped into the passes, and reported to the emperor, "I killed a Joseon general.

sentences.zh: 」上為其名美，即不詰，拜何為遼東東部都尉。

translations.literal: " The emperor, pleased with the name of the deed, did not question him and appointed He Governor of the Eastern Division of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, pleased with the deed's name, did not question him and appointed He Governor of the Eastern Division of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮怨何，發兵襲攻殺何。

translations.literal: Joseon resented He and sent troops to raid and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Joseon resented He and sent troops to raid and kill him.

sentences.zh: ----8六月，甘泉房中產芝九莖，上為之赦天下。

translations.literal: ----8 In the sixth month, nine stalks of mushroom grew in a room at Ganquan; the emperor thereupon proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 In the sixth month, nine stalks of mushroom grew in a room at Ganquan; the emperor proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----9上以旱為憂，公孫卿曰：「黃帝時，封則天旱，乾封三年。

translations.literal: ----9 The emperor was troubled by drought; Gongsun Qing said: "In the time of the Yellow Emperor, when the feng was performed there was drought; the Qianfeng lasted three years.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 The emperor was troubled by drought; Gongsun Qing said, "In the time of the Yellow Emperor, when the feng was performed there was drought; the Qianfeng lasted three years.

sentences.zh: 」上乃下詔曰：「天旱，意乾封乎！

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon issued an edict: "Heaven is dry—is it Qianfeng!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor issued an edict: "Heaven is dry—is it Qianfeng!

sentences.zh: 」----10秋，作明堂於汶上。

translations.literal: " ----10 In autumn, the Bright Hall was built on the Wen.
translations.idiomatic: " ----10 In autumn, the Bright Hall was built on the Wen.

sentences.zh: ----11上募天下死罪為兵，遣樓船將軍楊僕從齊浮渤海，左將軍荀彘出遼東，以討朝鮮。

translations.literal: ----11 The emperor recruited men under sentence of death from all under Heaven as soldiers, sent Tower-Ship General Yang Pu to float across the Bohai from Qi, and Left General Xun Zhi to march out from Liaodong to attack Joseon.
translations.idiomatic: ----11 The emperor recruited men under sentence of death from across the realm as soldiers, sent Tower-Ship General Yang Pu to sail from Qi across the Bohai, and Left General Xun Zhi out from Liaodong to attack Joseon.

sentences.zh: ----12初，上使-{王然于}-以越破及誅南夷兵威喻滇王入朝。

translations.literal: ----12 At the outset, the emperor sent -{Wang Ranyu}- with the military prestige of the defeat of Yue and the execution of the Southern Yi to instruct the King of Dian to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: ----12 At the outset the emperor sent Wang Ranyu with the military prestige of Yue's defeat and the Southern Yi's punishment to persuade the King of Dian to come to court.

sentences.zh: 滇王者，其眾數萬人，其旁東北有勞深、靡莫，皆同姓相杖，未肯聽。

translations.literal: The King of Dian had a host of several tens of thousands; to his northeast were Laoshen and Mimuo, all of the same surname supporting one another, who had not yet been willing to obey.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dian had tens of thousands of followers; to his northeast were Laoshen and Mimuo, clansmen who supported one another and would not yet obey.

sentences.zh: 勞深、靡莫數侵犯使者吏卒。

translations.literal: Laoshen and Mimuo repeatedly encroached upon and attacked the envoys' clerks and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshen and Mimuo repeatedly attacked the envoys' clerks and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 於是上遣將軍郭昌、中郎將衛廣發巴、蜀兵擊滅勞深、靡莫，以兵臨滇。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor sent General Guo Chang and Palace Gentleman-Commandant Wei Guang to raise troops from Ba and Shu, strike and destroy Laoshen and Mimuo, and press the army against Dian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent General Guo Chang and Palace Gentleman-Commandant Wei Guang to raise Ba and Shu troops, destroy Laoshen and Mimuo, and press the army against Dian.

sentences.zh: 滇王舉國降，請置吏入朝，於是以為益州郡，賜滇王王印，復長其民。

translations.literal: The King of Dian surrendered with his whole state, requested that officials be set over him and that he enter court; thereupon it was made Yizhou Commandery, the King of Dian was given a king's seal, and he was again made to rule his people.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dian surrendered his whole state, asked for officials and permission to come to court; it was made Yizhou Commandery, the king was given a royal seal, and he was again made to rule his people.

sentences.zh: 是時，漢滅兩越，平西南夷，置初郡十七，且以其故俗治，毋賦稅。

translations.literal: At this time Han had destroyed the two Yues and pacified the Southwestern Yi, establishing seventeen new commanderies, governing them by their old customs and levying no taxes.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Han had destroyed the two Yues and pacified the Southwestern Yi, establishing seventeen new commanderies, governing them by their old customs and levying no taxes.

sentences.zh: 南陽、漢中以往郡，各以地比，給初郡吏卒奉食、幣物、傳車、馬被具。

translations.literal: The commanderies from Nanyang and Hanzhong westward each according to proximity supplied the new commanderies' officials and soldiers with rations, goods, relay carts, horses, and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies from Nanyang and Hanzhong westward each according to proximity supplied the new commanderies' officials and soldiers with rations, goods, relay carts, horses, and equipment.

sentences.zh: 而初郡時時小反，殺吏，漢發南方吏卒往誅之，間歲萬餘人，費皆仰給大農。

translations.literal: But the new commanderies from time to time rebelled on a small scale and killed officials; Han sent southern officials and soldiers to execute them—every other year more than ten thousand men—and the expense all depended on the Grand Agriculture Minister.
translations.idiomatic: But the new commanderies rebelled in small outbreaks and killed officials; Han sent southern troops to punish them—more than ten thousand men every other year—and the expense all fell on the Grand Agriculture Minister.

sentences.zh: 大農以均輸、調鹽鐵助賦，故能贍之。

translations.literal: The Grand Agriculture Minister, with equalizing transport and the salt-and-iron adjustments aiding the levies, was therefore able to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Agriculture Minister, aided by equalizing transport and salt-and-iron adjustments, was able to meet the cost.

sentences.zh: 然兵所過，縣為以訾給毋乏而已，不也言擅賦法矣。

translations.literal: Yet where the army passed, the districts merely assessed supplies so there would be no shortage—that was all; they did not also speak of unauthorized tax statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet where the army passed, districts merely assessed supplies so there would be no shortage—that was all; they dared not speak of unauthorized levies.

sentences.zh: ----13是歲，以御史中丞南陽杜周為廷尉。

translations.literal: ----13 That year, Du Zhou of Nanyang, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was made Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: ----13 That year Du Zhou of Nanyang, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was made Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 周外寬，內深次骨，其治大放張湯。

translations.literal: Zhou was outwardly lenient but inwardly deep to the bone; his governance greatly followed Zhang Tang's model.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was outwardly lenient but inwardly ruthless; his governance greatly followed Zhang Tang's model.

sentences.zh: 時詔獄益多，二千石系者，新故相因，不減百餘人；

translations.literal: At that time imperial-prison cases grew ever more numerous; those imprisoned at the two-thousand-bushel rank, new and old succeeding one another, were no fewer than a hundred-odd;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial-prison cases grew ever more numerous; officials at the two-thousand-bushel rank in custody, new and old succeeding one another, numbered no fewer than a hundred;

sentences.zh: 廷尉一歲至千餘章，章大者連逮證案數百，小者數十人；

translations.literal: the Commandant of Justice in one year received more than a thousand memorials; in large cases the connected arrests and evidence ran to several hundred, in small ones to several tens;
translations.idiomatic: the Commandant of Justice in one year received more than a thousand cases; large cases involved hundreds in connected arrests, small ones dozens;

sentences.zh: 遠者數千、近者數百里會獄。

translations.literal: those from afar several thousand, those from near several hundred li, were gathered for trial.
translations.idiomatic: defendants were gathered for trial from thousands of li away, or from hundreds.

sentences.zh: 廷尉及中都官詔獄逮至六七萬人，吏所增加，十萬餘人。

translations.literal: Those arrested in the Commandant of Justice's and the capital officials' imperial prisons reached sixty or seventy thousand; with those the clerks added, more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Those arrested in the Commandant of Justice's and capital officials' imperial prisons reached sixty or seventy thousand; with those the clerks added, more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十二月，雷；

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the twelfth month, there was thunder;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the twelfth month, there was thunder;

sentences.zh: 雨雹，大如馬頭。

translations.literal: hail fell as large as horses' heads.
translations.idiomatic: hail fell as large as horses' heads.

sentences.zh: ----2上遣將軍趙破奴擊車師。

translations.literal: ----2 The emperor sent General Zhao Poniang to attack the Wusun state of Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 The emperor sent General Zhao Poniang to attack Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 破奴與輕騎七百餘先至，虜樓蘭王，遂破車師，因舉兵威以困烏孫、大宛之屬。

translations.literal: Poniang with more than seven hundred light cavalry arrived first, captured the King of Loulan, then broke Cheshi, and thereby raised military prestige to press Wusun, Dayuan, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Poniang with more than seven hundred light cavalry arrived first, captured the King of Loulan, broke Cheshi, and raised military prestige to press Wusun, Dayuan, and the like.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲申，封破奴為浞野侯。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiashen, Poniang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuoye.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiashen, Poniang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuoye.

sentences.zh: 王恢佐破奴擊樓蘭，封恢為浩侯。

translations.literal: Wang Hui assisted Poniang in attacking Loulan and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui assisted Poniang in attacking Loulan and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hao.

sentences.zh: 於是酒泉列亭障至玉門矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Jiuquan beacon towers and barriers were set in line as far as Jade Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon beacon towers and barriers were set in line from Jiuquan as far as Jade Gate.

sentences.zh: ----3初作角抵戲、魚龍曼延之屬。

translations.literal: ----3 For the first time wrestling contests and fish-dragon spreading displays and the like were performed.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 For the first time wrestling contests and fish-dragon pageants and the like were performed.

sentences.zh: ----4漢兵入朝鮮境，朝鮮王右渠發兵距險。

translations.literal: ----4 Han troops entered Joseon territory; King Youqu of Joseon sent troops to hold the passes.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 Han troops entered Joseon; King Youqu sent troops to hold the passes.

sentences.zh: 樓船將軍將齊兵七千人先至王險。

translations.literal: Tower-Ship General led seven thousand Qi troops and arrived first at Wangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Tower-Ship General led seven thousand Qi troops and arrived first at Wangxian.

sentences.zh: 右渠城守，窺知樓船軍少，即出城擊樓船；

translations.literal: Youqu defended the city; spying and learning that the tower-ship army was few, he at once came out and attacked the tower-ships;
translations.idiomatic: Youqu defended the city; seeing the tower-ship force was small, he sallied out to attack them;

sentences.zh: 樓船軍敗散，遁山中十餘日，稍求退散卒，復聚。

translations.literal: the tower-ship army was defeated and scattered, hid in the mountains more than ten days, gradually sought out the scattered soldiers who had retreated, and gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: the tower-ship army was defeated and scattered, hid in the mountains more than ten days, gradually gathered the scattered survivors, and re-formed.

sentences.zh: 左將軍擊朝鮮浿水西軍，未能破。

translations.literal: Left General attacked the Joseon army west of the Yalu but could not break it.
translations.idiomatic: Left General attacked the Joseon army west of the Yalu but could not break it.

sentences.zh: 天子為兩將未有利，乃使衛山因兵威往諭右渠。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, because the two generals had no success, sent Wei Shan with military prestige to go instruct Youqu.
translations.idiomatic: Because the two generals had no success, the emperor sent Wei Shan with the army's prestige to instruct Youqu.

sentences.zh: 右渠見使者，頓首謝：「願降，恐兩將詐殺臣，今見信節，請復降。

translations.literal: Youqu met the envoy, knocked his head and apologized: "I wish to surrender but fear the two generals will deceive and kill me; now seeing the credentials of trust, I beg to surrender again.
translations.idiomatic: Youqu met the envoy, knocked his head and said, "I wish to surrender but fear the two generals will trick and kill me; now seeing your credentials of trust, I beg to surrender again.

sentences.zh: 」遣太子入謝，獻馬五千匹，及饋軍糧；

translations.literal: " He sent the heir to enter and apologize, presenting five thousand horses and provisions for the army;
translations.idiomatic: " He sent the crown prince to apologize in person, presenting five thousand horses and army provisions;

sentences.zh: 人眾萬餘，持兵方渡浿水。

translations.literal: more than ten thousand men, armed, were just crossing the Yalu.
translations.idiomatic: more than ten thousand armed men were just crossing the Yalu.

sentences.zh: 使者及左將軍疑其為變，謂太子：「已服降，宜令人毋持兵。

translations.literal: The envoy and Left General suspected treachery and told the heir: "Having submitted, you ought to have your men not bear arms.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy and Left General suspected treachery and told the crown prince, "Having submitted, you ought to order your men not to bear arms.

sentences.zh: 」太子亦疑使者、左將軍詐殺之，遂不渡浿水，復引歸。

translations.literal: " The heir also suspected the envoy and Left General would deceive and kill him, and therefore did not cross the Yalu but led his men back.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince also suspected the envoy and Left General would trick and kill him, and did not cross the Yalu but led his men back.

sentences.zh: 山還報天子，天子誅山。

translations.literal: Shan returned and reported to the Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven executed Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Shan returned and reported; the emperor executed Shan.

sentences.zh: 左將軍破浿水上軍，乃前至城下，圍其西北，樓船亦往會，居城南。

translations.literal: Left General broke the Joseon army above the Yalu, then advanced to below the city, besieging the northwest; the tower-ships also went to join him and encamped south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Left General broke the Joseon army above the Yalu, advanced to the city, besieged the northwest, and the tower-ships joined him south of the city.

sentences.zh: 右渠遂堅守城，數月未能下。

translations.literal: Youqu thereupon held the city firmly; for months it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Youqu held the city firmly; for months it could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 左將軍所將燕、代卒多勁悍，樓船將齊卒已嘗敗亡困辱，卒皆恐，將心慚，其圍右渠，常持和節。

translations.literal: The Yan and Dai soldiers under Left General were mostly fierce and strong; the Qi soldiers under the tower-ship general had already suffered defeat, flight, and humiliation—the soldiers were all afraid and the general's heart ashamed; in besieging Youqu they constantly held to conciliatory measures.
translations.idiomatic: Left General's Yan and Dai troops were mostly fierce; the tower-ship general's Qi troops had already suffered defeat and humiliation—the soldiers were afraid and the general ashamed; in besieging Youqu they constantly held to conciliation.

sentences.zh: 左將軍急擊之，朝鮮大臣乃陰間使人私約降樓船，往來言尚未肯決。

translations.literal: Left General pressed the attack hotly; Joseon ministers thereupon sent men in secret to arrange surrender privately with the tower-ships, going back and forth—word had not yet been settled.
translations.idiomatic: Left General pressed the attack; Joseon ministers secretly sent men to arrange surrender with the tower-ships, going back and forth—nothing was yet settled.

sentences.zh: 左將軍數與樓船期戰，樓船欲就其約，不會。

translations.literal: Left General repeatedly set dates with the tower-ships for battle; the tower-ships wished to follow their pact and did not join.
translations.idiomatic: Left General repeatedly set dates for joint battle; the tower-ships wished to honor their pact and did not join.

sentences.zh: 左將軍亦使人求間隙降下朝鮮，朝鮮不肯，心附樓船，以故兩將不相能。

translations.literal: Left General also sent men seeking an opening to bring Joseon down in surrender; Joseon would not, their hearts attached to the tower-ships—for this reason the two generals could not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Left General also sent men seeking an opening to accept surrender; Joseon would not, their hearts with the tower-ships—for this reason the two generals could not cooperate.

sentences.zh: 左將軍心意樓船前有失軍罪，今與朝鮮私善，而又不降，疑其有反計，未敢發。

translations.literal: Left General thought in his heart that the tower-ships had earlier the crime of losing the army, now were on private good terms with Joseon, and yet did not surrender—he suspected them of a plot to rebel and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Left General thought the tower-ships had earlier lost the army, now were on private terms with Joseon, and yet did not surrender—he suspected treason and did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 天子以兩將圍城乖異，兵久不決，使濟南太守公孫遂往正之，有便宜得以從事。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, because the two generals besieging the city were at odds and the army long undecided, sent the Governor of Jinan Gongsun Sui to correct them, with authority to act as expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Because the two generals besieging the city were at odds and the army long undecided, the emperor sent Governor of Jinan Gongsun Sui to correct them, with authority to act as expedient.

sentences.zh: 遂至，左將軍曰：「朝鮮當下，久之不下者，樓船數期不會。

translations.literal: When Sui arrived, Left General said: "Joseon ought to fall; the reason it has long not fallen is that the tower-ships repeatedly set dates and did not join.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui arrived, Left General said, "Joseon ought to have fallen; the reason it has not is that the tower-ships repeatedly set dates and did not join.

sentences.zh: 」具以素所意告，曰：「今如此不取，恐為大害。

translations.literal: " He fully told what he had long thought and said: "If we do not seize them now like this, I fear it will be a great harm.
translations.idiomatic: " He fully told his long-held suspicions and said, "If we do not seize them now, I fear great harm.

sentences.zh: 」遂亦以為然，乃以節召樓船將軍入左將軍營計事，即命左將軍麾下執樓船將軍，并其軍。

translations.literal: " Sui also thought it so; he thereupon with credentials summoned the tower-ship general into Left General's camp to consult, and at once ordered Left General's subordinates to seize the tower-ship general and merge his army.
translations.idiomatic: " Sui agreed; he summoned the tower-ship general into Left General's camp to consult, and at once ordered Left General's men to seize him and merge his army.

sentences.zh: 以報天子，天子誅遂。

translations.literal: He reported to the Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven executed Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the emperor; the emperor executed Sui.

sentences.zh: 左將軍已并兩軍，即急擊朝鮮。

translations.literal: Left General having merged the two armies, at once pressed the attack on Joseon.
translations.idiomatic: Left General, having merged the two armies, at once pressed the attack on Joseon.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮相路人、相韓陰、尼谿相參、將軍王唊相與謀曰：「始欲降樓船，樓船今執，獨左將軍並將，戰益急，恐不能與戰；

translations.literal: Joseon chancellor Luren, chancellor Han Yin, Nixi chancellor Can, and general Wang Jia together plotted, saying: "At first we wished to surrender to the tower-ships; the tower-ships are now seized; only Left General commands the merged armies and the fighting grows fiercer—we fear we cannot fight;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Luren and Han Yin, Nixi Chancellor Can, and General Wang Jia plotted together, saying, "At first we wished to surrender to the tower-ships; the tower-ships are now seized; only Left General commands the merged armies and fighting grows fiercer—we fear we cannot fight;

sentences.zh: 王又不肯降。

translations.literal: the king also will not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: the king also will not surrender.

sentences.zh: 」陰、唊、路人皆亡降漢，路人道死。

translations.literal: " Yin, Jia, and Luren all fled and surrendered to Han; Luren died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin, Jia, and Luren all fled and surrendered to Han; Luren died on the road.

sentences.zh: 夏，尼谿參使人殺朝鮮王右渠來降。

translations.literal: In summer, Can of Nixi sent men to kill King Youqu of Joseon and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, Can of Nixi sent men to kill King Youqu and came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 王險城未下，故右渠之大臣成己又反，復攻吏。

translations.literal: Wangxian city was not yet taken; therefore Youqu's minister Cheng Ji rebelled again and attacked the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wangxian was not yet taken; Youqu's minister Cheng Ji rebelled again and attacked the officials.

sentences.zh: 左將軍使右渠子長、降相路人之子最告諭其民。

translations.literal: Left General sent Youqu's son Chang and the surrendered chancellor Luren's son Zui to announce and instruct the people.
translations.idiomatic: Left General sent Youqu's son Chang and the surrendered chancellor Luren's son Zui to announce and instruct the people.

sentences.zh: 誅成己。

translations.literal: Cheng Ji was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji was executed.

sentences.zh: 以故遂定朝鮮，為樂浪、臨屯、玄菟、真番四郡。

translations.literal: For this reason Joseon was thereupon settled, made into the four commanderies of Lelang, Lintun, Xuantu, and Zhenfan.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Joseon was settled and made into the four commanderies of Lelang, Lintun, Xuantu, and Zhenfan.

sentences.zh: 封參為澅清侯，陰為萩苴侯，唊為平州侯，長為幾侯，最以父死頗有功，為涅陽侯。

translations.literal: Can was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huqing, Yin as Marquis of Qiuju, Jia as Marquis of Pingzhou, Chang as Marquis of Ji, and Zui because his father died and he had some merit was made Marquis of Nieyang.
translations.idiomatic: Can was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huqing, Yin as Marquis of Qiuju, Jia as Marquis of Pingzhou, Chang as Marquis of Ji, and Zui—his father having died with some merit—as Marquis of Nieyang.

sentences.zh: 左將軍徵至，坐爭功相嫉乖計，棄市。

translations.literal: When Left General was summoned back, he was convicted of contending for merit, mutual jealousy, and perverse planning, and abandoned in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When Left General was summoned back, he was convicted of contending for merit, mutual jealousy, and thwarting the plan, and executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 樓船將軍亦坐兵至列口，當待左將軍，擅先縱，失亡多，當誅，贖為庶人。

translations.literal: The tower-ship general was also convicted: his troops had reached Liekou and ought to have awaited Left General, but he rashly advanced first, lost many, and deserved execution; he ransomed his life and became a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The tower-ship general was also convicted: his troops had reached Liekou and ought to have awaited Left General, but he rashly advanced first and lost many men; he deserved execution but ransomed his life and became a commoner.

sentences.zh: :班固曰：玄菟、樂浪，本箕子所封。

translations.literal: : Ban Gu said: Xuantu and Lelang were originally the fiefs enfeoffed to Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: : Ban Gu said: Xuantu and Lelang were originally the fiefs enfeoffed to Jizi.

sentences.zh: 昔箕子居朝鮮，教其民以禮義，田蠶織作，為民設禁八條，相殺，以當時償殺；

translations.literal: In former times Jizi dwelt in Joseon and taught its people ritual and righteousness, field work, silkworms, weaving, and crafts; he set for the people eight prohibitions: for mutual killing, compensation with killing in turn;
translations.idiomatic: In former times Jizi dwelt in Joseon and taught its people ritual and righteousness, farming, sericulture, weaving, and crafts; he set eight prohibitions for the people: for mutual killing, compensation with killing in turn;

sentences.zh: 相傷，以穀償；

translations.literal: for mutual wounding, compensation with grain;
translations.idiomatic: for mutual wounding, compensation with grain;

sentences.zh: 相盜者，男沒入為其家奴，女為婢；

translations.literal: for mutual theft, the man was confiscated and made the other family's slave, the woman a maidservant;
translations.idiomatic: for mutual theft, the man was confiscated as the other family's slave, the woman as maidservant;

sentences.zh: 欲自贖者人五十萬，雖免為民，俗猶羞之，嫁娶無所售。

translations.literal: Those wishing to redeem themselves paid five hundred thousand per person; though freed to be commoners, custom still shamed them, and in marriage none would take them.
translations.idiomatic: Those wishing to redeem themselves paid five hundred thousand cash per person; though freed to commoner status, custom still shamed them, and no one would marry them.

sentences.zh: 是以其民終不相盜，無門戶之閉，婦人貞信不淫辟。

translations.literal: Therefore its people in the end did not steal from one another; there was no closing of doors and gates; women were chaste and faithful and did not go astray.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore its people did not steal from one another; doors and gates needed no closing; women were chaste and faithful and did not go astray.

sentences.zh: 其田野飲食以籩豆，都邑頗放效吏，往往以杯器食。

translations.literal: In the fields and countryside they ate and drank with platters and stands; in the capital cities they largely imitated officials, and often ate with cups and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the countryside they ate and drank from platters and stands; in the cities they largely imitated officials and often ate with cups and vessels.

sentences.zh: 郡初取吏於遼東，吏見民無閉臧，及賈人往者，夜則為盜，俗稍益薄，今於犯禁浸多，至六十餘條。

translations.literal: When the commandery first took clerks from Liaodong, the clerks saw the people did not close their stores, and when merchants went in, they stole by night; custom gradually grew thinner, and now violations of prohibitions have gradually increased to more than sixty articles.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery first took clerks from Liaodong, the clerks saw the people did not lock their stores, and when merchants came they stole by night; custom gradually grew lax, and now violations of prohibitions have increased to more than sixty articles.

sentences.zh: 可貴哉，仁賢之化也！

translations.literal: How admirable! The transformation of benevolence and worthiness!
translations.idiomatic: How admirable—the transformation wrought by benevolence and worthiness!

sentences.zh: 然東夷天性柔順，異於三方之外。

translations.literal: Yet the Eastern Yi by nature are gentle and compliant, unlike those outside the three directions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Eastern Yi are by nature gentle and compliant, unlike the peoples beyond the three directions.

sentences.zh: 故孔子悼道不行，設浮桴於海，欲居九夷，有以也夫！

translations.literal: Therefore when Confucius grieved that the Way did not prevail, he set a raft on the sea and wished to dwell among the Nine Yi—there was reason in it!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Confucius grieved that the Way did not prevail, he spoke of setting a raft on the sea and dwelling among the Nine Yi—there was reason in it!

sentences.zh: ----5秋，七月，膠西於王端薨。

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, the seventh month, King Duan of Jiaoxi Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, the seventh month, King Duan of Jiaoxi Yu died.

sentences.zh: ----6武都氐反，分徙酒泉。

translations.literal: ----6 The Di of Wudu rebelled; they were dispersed and relocated to Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 The Di of Wudu rebelled; they were dispersed and relocated to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，上行幸雍，祠五畤。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.

sentences.zh: 通回中道，遂北出蕭關。

translations.literal: He opened the road through Huizhong, then went north out through Xiaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the road through Huizhong, then went north out through Xiaoguan.

sentences.zh: 歷獨鹿、鳴澤，自代而還，幸河東。

translations.literal: He passed through Dulu and Ming Marsh, returned from Dai, and favored Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through Dulu and Ming Marsh, returned from Dai, and traveled in favor to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，祠后土，赦汾陰、夏陽、中都死罪以下。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, he sacrificed to the Earth Lord and pardoned those below death offense in Fenyin, Xiayang, and Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, he sacrificed to the Earth Lord and pardoned those below death offense in Fenyin, Xiayang, and Zhongdu.

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, there was great drought.

sentences.zh: ----3匈奴自衛、霍度幕以來，希復為寇，遠徙北方，休養士馬，習射獵，數使使於漢，好辭甘言求請和親。

translations.literal: ----3 Since Wei and Huo crossed the desert curtain, the Xiongnu rarely raided again; they moved far to the north, rested troops and horses, practiced archery and hunting, and repeatedly sent envoys to Han with pleasing words and sweet speech seeking peace marriage.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Since Wei and Huo crossed the desert curtain, the Xiongnu rarely raided again; they moved far north, rested troops and horses, practiced archery and hunting, and repeatedly sent envoys to Han with pleasing words seeking a peace marriage.

sentences.zh: 漢使北地人王烏等窺匈奴，烏從其俗，去節入穹廬，單于愛之，佯許甘言，為遣其太子入漢為質。

translations.literal: Han sent Wang Wu of Beidi and others to spy on the Xiongnu; Wu followed their custom, removed his staff of office and entered the yurt; the Chanyu favored him and falsely promised sweet words, undertaking to send his crown prince into Han as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Wang Wu of Beidi and others to reconnoiter the Xiongnu; Wu followed their custom, removed his staff of office and entered the yurt; the Chanyu favored him and falsely promised sweet words, undertaking to send his crown prince into Han as hostage.

sentences.zh: 漢使楊信於匈奴，信不肯從其俗，單于曰：「故約漢嘗遣翁主，給繒絮食物有品，以和親，而匈奴亦不擾邊。

translations.literal: Han sent Yang Xin to the Xiongnu; Xin would not follow their custom; the Chanyu said: "By the old agreement Han once sent a princess, supplied silk floss and food in fixed grades for peace marriage, and the Xiongnu also did not disturb the border.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Yang Xin to the Xiongnu; Xin would not follow their custom; the Chanyu said, "By the old agreement Han once sent a princess, supplied silk floss and food in fixed grades for a peace marriage, and the Xiongnu also did not disturb the border.

sentences.zh: 今乃欲反古，令吾太子為質，無幾矣。

translations.literal: Now you wish to turn back the ancient way and make my crown prince a hostage—there is little hope of it.
translations.idiomatic: Now you wish to turn back the ancient way and make my crown prince a hostage—there is little hope of it.

sentences.zh: 」信既歸，漢又使王烏往，而單于復諂以甘言，欲多得漢財物，紿謂王烏曰：「吾欲入漢見天子面，相約為兄弟。

translations.literal: " After Xin returned, Han again sent Wang Wu; the Chanyu again flattered with sweet words, wishing to obtain more Han goods, and deceived Wu, saying: "I wish to enter Han and see the Son of Heaven face to face and covenant as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: " After Xin returned, Han again sent Wang Wu; the Chanyu again flattered with sweet words, wishing to obtain more Han goods, and deceived Wu, saying, "I wish to enter Han and see the Son of Heaven face to face and covenant as brothers.

sentences.zh: 」王烏歸報漢，漢為單于築邸於長安。

translations.literal: " Wu returned and reported to Han; Han built a residence for the Chanyu in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " Wu returned and reported to Han; Han built a residence for the Chanyu in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 匈奴曰：「非得漢貴人使，吾不與誠語。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu said: "Unless I get a Han noble envoy, I will not speak sincerely with you.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu said, "Unless I get a Han noble envoy, I will not speak sincerely with you.

sentences.zh: 」匈奴使其貴人至漢，病，漢予藥，欲愈之，不幸而死。

translations.literal: " The Xiongnu sent their noble to Han; he fell ill; Han gave medicine wishing to cure him, but unluckily he died.
translations.idiomatic: " The Xiongnu sent their noble to Han; he fell ill; Han gave medicine wishing to cure him, but unluckily he died.

sentences.zh: 漢使路充國佩二千石印綬往使，因送其喪，厚葬直數千金，曰：「此漢貴人也。

translations.literal: Han sent Lu Chongguo bearing a two-thousand-dan seal and cord as envoy, and thereby sent off his funeral; a lavish burial worth several thousand in gold was provided, saying: "This was a Han noble.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Lu Chongguo bearing a two-thousand-dan seal and cord as envoy and sent off his funeral; a lavish burial worth several thousand in gold was provided, saying, "This was a Han noble.

sentences.zh: 」單于以為漢殺吾貴使者，乃留路充國不歸。

translations.literal: " The Chanyu thought Han had killed his noble envoy and detained Lu Chongguo, not letting him return.
translations.idiomatic: " The Chanyu thought Han had killed his noble envoy and detained Lu Chongguo, not letting him return.

sentences.zh: 諸所言者，單于特空紿王烏，殊無意入漢及遣太子。

translations.literal: All that had been said—the Chanyu had merely deceived Wang Wu in vain; he had absolutely no intent to enter Han or send the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: All that had been said—the Chanyu had merely deceived Wang Wu in vain; he had absolutely no intent to enter Han or send the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 於是匈奴數使奇兵侵犯漢邊。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Xiongnu repeatedly sent raiding detachments to invade the Han border.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Xiongnu repeatedly sent raiding detachments to invade the Han border.

sentences.zh: 乃拜郭昌為拔胡將軍，及浞野侯屯朔方以東，備胡。

translations.literal: Guo Chang was then invested as General Who Uproots the Barbarians, and together with the Marquis of Zhuoye he encamped east of Shuofang to guard against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chang was then invested as General Who Uproots the Barbarians, and together with the Marquis of Zhuoye he encamped east of Shuofang to guard against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 1冬，上南巡狩，至於盛唐，望祀虞舜於九疑。

translations.literal: 1 In winter, the emperor made a southern imperial tour to Sheng Tang, gazed and sacrificed to Shun of Yu at Jiuyi.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the emperor made a southern imperial tour to Sheng Tang and gazed and sacrificed to Shun of Yu at Jiuyi.

sentences.zh: 登灊天柱山，自尋陽浮江，親射蛟江中，獲之。

translations.literal: He ascended Qian's Tianzhu Mountain, from Xunyang floated on the river, personally shot a flood dragon in the river, and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended Tianzhu Mountain in Qian, from Xunyang floated on the river, personally shot a flood dragon in the river, and obtained it.

sentences.zh: 舳艫千里，薄樅陽而出，遂北至琅邪，並海，所過禮祠其名山大川。

translations.literal: Warships stretched a thousand li; pressing Zongyang he went out, then north to Langya along the sea; wherever he passed he performed rites and sacrificed to famous mountains and great rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Warships stretched a thousand li; pressing Zongyang he went out, then north to Langya along the sea; wherever he passed he performed rites and sacrificed to famous mountains and great rivers.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，還至太山，增封。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, he returned to Mount Tai and increased the feng and shan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, he returned to Mount Tai and increased the feng and shan.

sentences.zh: 甲子，始祀上帝於明堂，配以高祖，因朝諸侯王、列侯，受郡、國計。

translations.literal: On jiazi he first sacrificed to the Supreme Lord in the Bright Hall, paired with Gaozu, and thereby received in audience the feudal kings, princes, and marquises and received the accounts of the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he first sacrificed to the Supreme Lord in the Bright Hall, paired with Gaozu, received in audience the feudal kings, princes, and marquises, and received the accounts of the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 還，幸甘泉，郊泰畤。

translations.idiomatic: A tomb mound was raised, modeled on Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: ----4上以名臣文武欲盡，乃下詔曰：「蓋有非常之功，必待非常之人。

translations.idiomatic: Therefore a horse may kick and rear yet run a thousand li; a gentleman may bear the burden of vulgar opinion yet establish merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 夫泛駕之馬，跅弛之士，亦在御之而已。

translations.literal: As for horses hard to drive and unbridled gentlemen, it lies only in how one handles them.
translations.idiomatic: As for horses hard to drive and unbridled gentlemen, it lies only in how one handles them.

sentences.zh: 其令州、郡察吏、民有茂才、異等可為將、相及使絕國者。

translations.idiomatic: Let the provinces and commanderies examine officials and people for outstanding talent and exceptional ability fit to be generals, chancellors, or envoys to distant states.

translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor pardoned fugitives from the capital, ordered them to join the army, and dispatched General Who Uproots the Barbarians Guo Chang to lead troops against them; heads cut numbered several hundred thousand.

translations.literal: ----5 In autumn, great drought and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In autumn, there was great drought and locusts.

sentences.zh: ----6烏孫使者見漢廣大，歸報其國，其國乃益重漢。

translations.literal: ----6 Wusun envoys saw Han's vast extent; returning they reported to their state, and their state thereupon valued Han the more.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Wusun envoys saw Han's vast extent; returning they reported to their state, and their state thereupon valued Han the more.

sentences.zh: 匈奴聞烏孫與漢通，怒，欲擊之。

translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu heard Wusun communicated with Han, grew angry, and wished to attack them.

sentences.zh: 又其旁大宛、月氏之屬皆事漢，烏孫於是恐，使使願得尚漢公主，為昆弟。

translations.literal: Moreover Dayuan, the Yuezhi, and the like beside them all served Han; Wusun thereupon feared and sent envoys wishing to obtain marriage with a Han princess and become brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Dayuan, the Yuezhi, and the like beside them all served Han; Wusun thereupon feared and sent envoys wishing to obtain marriage with a Han princess and become brothers.

sentences.zh: 天子與群臣議，許之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven deliberated with his ministers and assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deliberated with his ministers and assented.

sentences.zh: 烏孫以千匹馬往聘漢女。

translations.literal: Wusun sent a thousand horses to betroth a Han woman.
translations.idiomatic: Wusun sent a thousand horses to betroth a Han woman.

sentences.zh: 漢以江都王建女細君為公主，往妻烏孫，贈送甚盛；

translations.literal: Han made the daughter of King Jian of Jiangdu, Xijun, a princess and sent her to marry Wusun with very lavish gifts;
translations.idiomatic: Han made the daughter of King Jian of Jiangdu, Xijun, a princess and sent her to marry Wusun with very lavish gifts;

sentences.zh: 烏孫王昆莫以為右夫人。

translations.literal: the King of Wusun Kunmo made her his right consort.
translations.idiomatic: the King of Wusun Kunmo made her his right consort.

sentences.zh: 匈奴亦遣女妻昆莫，以為左夫人。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu also sent a woman to marry Kunmo and made her left consort.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu also sent a woman to marry Kunmo and made her left consort.

sentences.zh: 公主自治宮室居，歲時一再與昆莫會，置酒飲食。

translations.literal: The princess on her own built a palace residence; once or twice a year she met Kunmo, set out wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: The princess built her own palace residence; once or twice a year she met Kunmo and set out wine and food.

sentences.zh: 昆莫年老，言語不通，公主悲愁思歸，天子聞而憐之，間歲遣使者以帷帳錦繡給遺焉。

translations.literal: Kunmo was old; speech did not communicate; the princess grieved and longed to return; the Son of Heaven heard and pitied her, and every other year sent envoys with curtains, brocades, and silks as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Kunmo was old; they could not communicate; the princess grieved and longed to return; the emperor heard and pitied her, and every other year sent envoys with curtains, brocades, and silks as gifts.

sentences.zh: 昆莫曰：「我老。

translations.literal: Kunmo said: "I am old.
translations.idiomatic: Kunmo said, "I am old.

sentences.zh: 」欲使其孫岑娶尚公主。

translations.literal: " He wished to have his grandson Cen marry and obtain the princess.
translations.idiomatic: " He wished to have his grandson Cen marry the princess.

sentences.zh: 公主不聽，上書言狀。

translations.literal: The princess would not consent and memorialized stating the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The princess would not consent and memorialized stating the circumstances.

sentences.zh: 天子報曰：「從其國俗，欲與烏孫共滅胡。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven replied: "Follow their state's custom; I wish to join with Wusun to destroy the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Follow their state's custom; I wish to join with Wusun to destroy the Hu.

sentences.zh: 」岑娶遂妻公主。

translations.literal: " Cen married and thereupon took the princess as wife.
translations.idiomatic: " Cen married and thereupon took the princess as wife.

sentences.zh: 昆莫死，岑娶代立，為昆彌。

translations.literal: Kunmo died; Cen married succeeded and was established as Kunmi.
translations.idiomatic: Kunmo died; Cen married succeeded and was established as Kunmi.

sentences.zh: 是時，漢使西逾蔥嶺，抵安息。

translations.literal: At this time Han envoys west crossed the Onion Mountains and reached Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Han envoys west crossed the Onion Mountains and reached Parthia.

sentences.zh: 安息發使，以大鳥卵及黎軒善眩人獻於漢，及諸小國驩潛、大益、車姑師、扜冞、蘇䪥之屬，皆隨漢使獻見天子，天子大悅。

translations.literal: Parthia sent envoys presenting to Han great bird eggs and Lixuan men skilled in illusion; and various small states Huanqian, Dayi, Chegushi, Yuanchen, Suxie, and the like all followed Han envoys to present themselves before the Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Parthia sent envoys presenting to Han ostrich eggs and Lixuan men skilled in illusion; and various small states Huanqian, Dayi, Chegushi, Yuanchen, Suxie, and the like all followed Han envoys to present themselves before the emperor; the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 西國使更來更去，天子每巡狩海上，悉從外國客，大都、多人則過之，散財帛以賞賜，厚具以饒給之，以覽示漢富厚焉。

translations.literal: Western states' envoys came and went repeatedly; whenever the Son of Heaven toured the seacoast he took all foreign guests along; where states were great and populous he passed them by; he scattered wealth and silks to reward and lavishly supplied them, to display Han's wealth and abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Western states' envoys came and went repeatedly; whenever the emperor toured the seacoast he took all foreign guests along; where states were great and populous he passed them by; he scattered wealth and silks to reward and lavishly supplied them, to display Han's wealth and abundance.

sentences.zh: 大角抵，出奇戲、諸怪物，多聚觀者。

translations.literal: Great wrestling contests were held, producing strange performances and various marvels; many gathered to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Great wrestling contests were held, producing strange performances and various marvels; many gathered to watch.

sentences.zh: 行賞賜，酒池肉林，令外國客遍觀名倉庫府藏之積，見漢之廣大，傾駭之。

translations.literal: He carried out rewards and gifts, wine pools and meat forests, and ordered foreign guests to view throughout the famous storehouses and treasury accumulations; seeing Han's vastness, they were utterly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out rewards and gifts, wine pools and meat forests, and ordered foreign guests to view throughout the famous storehouses and treasury accumulations; seeing Han's vastness, they were utterly astonished.

sentences.zh: 大宛左右多蒲萄，可以為酒；

translations.literal: Around Dayuan there was much grape, which could be made into wine;
translations.idiomatic: Around Dayuan there was much grape, which could be made into wine;

sentences.zh: 多苜蓿，天馬嗜之；

translations.literal: much alfalfa, which Heavenly Horses loved;
translations.idiomatic: much alfalfa, which Heavenly Horses loved;

sentences.zh: 漢使采其實以來，天子種之於離宮別觀旁，極望。

translations.literal: Han envoys gathered their fruit and brought them; the Son of Heaven planted them beside detached palaces and lodges, as far as the eye could see.
translations.idiomatic: Han envoys gathered their fruit and brought them; the emperor planted them beside detached palaces and lodges, as far as the eye could see.

sentences.zh: 然西域以近匈奴，常畏匈奴使，待之過於漢使焉。

translations.literal: Yet the Western Regions, being near the Xiongnu, constantly feared Xiongnu envoys and treated them above Han envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Western Regions, being near the Xiongnu, constantly feared Xiongnu envoys and treated them above Han envoys.

translations.literal: ----7 That year the Xiongnu Chanyu Wuwu died; his son Wushilu was established, young in years, titled "Child Chanyu."
translations.idiomatic: ----7 That year the Xiongnu Chanyu Wuwu died; his son Wushilu was established, young in years, titled "Child Chanyu."

sentences.zh: 自此之後，單于益西北徙，左方兵直雲中，右方直酒泉、敦煌郡。

translations.literal: From this onward the Chanyu moved ever further northwest; the left-wing troops faced straight on Yunzhong, the right-wing straight on Jiuquan and Dunhuang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: From this onward the Chanyu moved ever further northwest; the left-wing troops faced Yunzhong, the right-wing Jiuquan and Dunhuang commanderies.

translations.idiomatic: 1 In winter, the tenth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲子朔旦，冬至，祠上帝於明堂。

translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day jiazi at dawn at the winter solstice, he sacrificed to the Supreme Lord in the Bright Hall.

translations.idiomatic: East to the seacoast, he examined those who entered the sea and method masters seeking spirits—none were verified;

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jianzhang Palace was built, measured at a thousand gates and ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Jianzhang Palace was built, measured at a thousand gates and ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其東則鳳闕，高二十餘丈；

translations.literal: To its east was Phoenix Tower, more than twenty zhang high;
translations.idiomatic: To its east was Phoenix Tower, more than twenty zhang high;

sentences.zh: 其西則唐中，數十里虎圈；

translations.literal: to its west Tangzhong, with a tiger park several tens of li;
translations.idiomatic: to its west Tangzhong, with a tiger park several tens of li;

translations.literal: to its north a great pool was made; the Gradual Terrace was more than twenty zhang high, named Grand Liquid Pool, with within it Penglai, Fangzhang, Yingzhou, and Huliang, representing sea divine mountains, turtles, fish, and the like;

sentences.zh: 其南有玉堂、璧門、大鳥之屬。

translations.literal: to its south were Jade Hall, Jade Gate, Great Bird, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: to its south were Jade Hall, Jade Gate, Great Bird, and the like.

sentences.zh: 立神明台、井幹樓，度五十丈，輦道相屬焉。

translations.literal: Spirit Bright Terrace and Well Canopy Tower were erected, measuring fifty zhang, with imperial carriage roads linking one to another.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit Bright Terrace and Well Canopy Tower were erected, measuring fifty zhang, with imperial carriage roads linking one to another.

translations.idiomatic: ----4 Grand Master Gongsun Qing, Hu Sui, Grand Astrologer Sima Qian, and others said, "The calendar's records are ruined and abolished; the era name and first month should be corrected.

sentences.zh: 」上詔兒寬與博士賜等共議，以為宜用夏正。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered Er Kuan together with Academician Ci and others to deliberate jointly; they considered that the Xia first month should be used.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Er Kuan together with Academician Ci and others to deliberate jointly; they considered that the Xia first month should be used.

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Qing, Sui, Qian, and others were ordered jointly to compose Han's Taichu Calendar, taking the first month as year start, color exalting yellow, numbers using five, fixing official titles, harmonizing pitch pipes, fixing the rites of the ancestral temple and the hundred offices, taking these as canonical constants to hand down to later generations -{云}-.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Qing, Sui, Qian, and others were ordered jointly to compose Han's Taichu Calendar, taking the first month as year start, exalting the color yellow, using the number five, fixing official titles, harmonizing pitch pipes, fixing the rites of the ancestral temple and the hundred offices, taking these as canonical constants to hand down to later generations -{云}-.

translations.literal: ----5 The Xiongnu Child Chanyu loved killing and campaigning; the people of the state were uneasy;
translations.idiomatic: ----5 The Xiongnu Child Chanyu loved killing and campaigning; the people of the state were uneasy;

sentences.zh: 又有天災，畜多死。

translations.literal: there was also a heaven-sent disaster; livestock mostly died.
translations.idiomatic: there was also a heaven-sent disaster; livestock mostly died.

translations.idiomatic: The Left Grand Commandant sent a man secretly to inform Han, saying, "I wish to kill the Chanyu and surrender to Han; Han is far—if troops come at once to welcome me, I will rise.

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon dispatched General Yinyu Gongsun Ao to build the Surrender-Receiving City outside the passes to respond.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon dispatched General Yinyu Gongsun Ao to build the Surrender-Receiving City outside the passes to respond.

translations.literal: ----6 In autumn, the eighth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In autumn, the eighth month, the emperor traveled in favor to Anding.

sentences.zh: ----7漢使入西域者言：「宛有善馬，在貳師城，匿不肯與漢使。

translations.literal: ----7 Han envoys who had entered the Western Regions said: "Yuan has fine horses at Ershi City; they hide them and refuse to give them to Han envoys.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 Han envoys who had entered the Western Regions said, "Yuan has fine horses at Ershi City; they hide them and refuse to give them to Han envoys.

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven sent stalwarts Che Ling and others bearing a thousand in gold and a golden horse to request them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent stalwarts Che Ling and others bearing a thousand in gold and a golden horse to request them.

sentences.zh: 宛王與其群臣謀曰：「漢去我遠，而鹽水中數敗，出其北有胡寇，出其南乏水草，又且往往而絕邑，乏食者多，漢使數百人為輩來，而常乏食，死者過半，是安能致大軍乎！

translations.literal: The King of Dayuan consulted with his ministers, saying: "Han is far from us, and in the Saltwater region they are repeatedly defeated; going out to the north there are Hu raiders; going out to the south there is lack of water and grass; moreover along the way towns are often cut off, and many lack food. Han envoys come in parties of several hundred, yet often lack food—more than half die. How could they possibly bring a great army!
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dayuan consulted with his ministers, saying, "Han is far from us, and in the Saltwater region they are repeatedly defeated; going out to the north there are Hu raiders; going out to the south there is lack of water and grass; moreover along the way towns are often cut off, and many lack food.
