sentences.zh: 天子業出兵誅宛，宛小國而不能下，則大夏之屬漸輕漢，而宛善馬絕不來，烏孫、輪台易苦漢使，為外國笑，乃案言伐宛尤不便者鄧光等。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had already raised troops to punish Dayuan; if a small state like Dayuan could not be taken, then the Da Yuezhi and their kind would gradually slight Han, Dayuan's good horses would never come, Wusun and Luntai would readily distress Han envoys, and foreign states would laugh—thereupon he prosecuted Deng Guang and others who had said attacking Dayuan was especially inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven had already raised troops to punish Dayuan; if a small state like Dayuan could not be taken, then the Da Yuezhi and their kind would gradually slight Han, Dayuan's good horses would never come, Wusun and Luntai would readily distress Han envoys, and foreign states would laugh—thereupon he prosecuted Deng Guang and others who had said attacking Dayuan was especially inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 赦囚徒，發惡少年及邊騎，歲餘而出敦煌者六萬人，負私從者不與，牛十萬，馬三萬匹，驢、橐駝以萬數，繼糧、兵弩甚設。

translations.literal: He pardoned convicts, raised vicious youths and border horsemen; after more than a year those who went out from Dunhuang were sixty thousand; private followers who bore their own supplies were not counted; cattle one hundred thousand, horses thirty thousand, donkeys and Bactrian camels by the tens of thousands; relay grain and weapons and crossbows were abundantly provided.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned convicts and raised vicious youths and border horsemen; after more than a year those who went out from Dunhuang were sixty thousand; private followers who bore their own supplies were not counted; cattle one hundred thousand, horses thirty thousand, donkeys and Bactrian camels by the tens of thousands; relay grain and weapons and crossbows were abundantly provided.

sentences.zh: 天下騷動，轉相奉伐宛五十餘校尉。

translations.literal: All under Heaven was in turmoil; relays supplied one another for the attack on Dayuan—over fifty colonels.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven was in turmoil; relays supplied one another for the attack on Dayuan—over fifty colonels.

sentences.zh: 宛城中無井，汲城外流水，於是遣水工徙其城下水，空以穴其城。

translations.literal: Within Dayuan city there were no wells; they drew flowing water outside the walls; thereupon he sent water engineers to divert the water below the city and tunnel into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Within Dayuan city there were no wells; they drew flowing water outside the walls; thereupon he sent water engineers to divert the water below the city and tunnel into the city.

sentences.zh: 益發戍甲卒十八萬酒泉、張掖北，置居延、休屠屯兵以衛酒泉，而發天下吏有罪者、亡命者及贅婿、賈人、故有市籍、父母大父母有市籍者凡七科，適為兵；

translations.literal: He further raised one hundred eighty thousand garrison armor-clad troops north of Jiuquan and Zhangye, stationed troops at Juyan and Xiutu to guard Jiuquan, and raised from all under Heaven officials guilty of offenses, fugitives, sons-in-law living with wives' families, merchants, those formerly on market registers, and those whose parents or great-grandparents had market registers—in all seven categories—assigning them as soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: He further raised one hundred eighty thousand garrison armor-clad troops north of Jiuquan and Zhangye, stationed troops at Juyan and Xiutu to guard Jiuquan, and raised from all under Heaven officials guilty of offenses, fugitives, sons-in-law living with wives' families, merchants, those formerly on market registers, and those whose parents or great-grandparents had market registers—in all seven categories—assigning them as soldiers;

sentences.zh: 及載糒給貳師，轉車人徒相連屬；

translations.literal: and those who carried grain to supply the Ershi—cart men and porters linked in continuous files;
translations.idiomatic: and those who carried grain to supply the Ershi—cart men and porters linked in continuous files;

sentences.zh: 而拜習馬者二人為執、驅馬校尉，備破宛擇取其善馬-{云}-。

translations.literal: he appointed two men skilled in horses as colonels of holding and driving horses, prepared for when Dayuan was broken to select its good horses -{yun}-.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed two men skilled in horses as colonels of holding and driving horses, prepared for when Dayuan was broken to select its good horses -{yun}-.

sentences.zh: 於是貳師後復行，兵多，所至小國莫不迎，出食給軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ershi again marched; the army was large; every small state reached did not fail to welcome them and put out food to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Ershi again marched; the army was large; every small state reached did not fail to welcome them and put out food to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 至輪台，輪台不下。

translations.literal: Reaching Luntai, Luntai would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Luntai, Luntai would not submit.

sentences.zh: 攻數日，屠之。

translations.literal: After several days of attack they slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: After several days of attack they slaughtered it.

sentences.zh: 自此而西，平行至宛城，兵到者三萬。

translations.literal: From here west they marched levelly to Dayuan city; troops who arrived were thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: From here west they marched levelly to Dayuan city; troops who arrived were thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 宛兵迎擊漢兵，漢兵射敗之，宛兵走入，保其城。

translations.literal: Dayuan troops met and struck Han troops; Han troops shot and defeated them; Dayuan troops ran in and held their city.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan troops met and struck Han troops; Han troops shot and defeated them; Dayuan troops ran in and held their city.

sentences.zh: 貳師欲攻郁成城，恐留行而令宛益生詐，乃先至宛，決其水原移之，則宛固已憂困，圍其城，攻之四十餘日。

translations.literal: The Ershi wished to attack Yucheng city, fearing that lingering on the march would let Dayuan grow more deceitful; he therefore went first to Dayuan, cut and diverted its water source, so that Dayuan was already anxious and distressed; he besieged the city and attacked over forty days.
translations.idiomatic: The Ershi wished to attack Yucheng city, fearing that lingering on the march would let Dayuan grow more deceitful; he therefore went first to Dayuan, cut and diverted its water source, so that Dayuan was already anxious and distressed; he besieged the city and attacked for over forty days.

sentences.zh: 宛貴人謀曰：「王毋寡匿善馬，殺漢使，今殺王而出善馬，漢兵宜解；

translations.literal: Dayuan nobles deliberated, saying: "King Wugua hid good horses and killed Han envoys; now if we kill the king and produce good horses, Han troops should withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan nobles deliberated, saying, "King Wugua hid good horses and killed Han envoys; now if we kill the king and produce good horses, Han troops should withdraw;

sentences.zh: 即不解，乃力戰而死，未晚也。

translations.literal: if they do not withdraw, then to fight with full strength and die is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: if they do not withdraw, then to fight with full strength and die is not yet late.

sentences.zh: 」宛貴人皆以為然，共殺王。

translations.literal: " The Dayuan nobles all thought it right and together killed the king.
translations.idiomatic: " The Dayuan nobles all thought it right and together killed the king.

sentences.zh: 其外城壞，虜宛貴人勇將煎靡。

translations.literal: The outer city was broken; they captured the Dayuan noble and brave general Jian Mi.
translations.idiomatic: The outer city was broken; they captured the Dayuan noble and brave general Jian Mi.

sentences.zh: 宛大恐，走入城中，持王毋寡頭，遣人使貳師，約曰：「漢無攻我，我盡出善馬恣所取，而給漢軍食。

translations.literal: Dayuan was greatly afraid, ran into the city, held King Wugua's head, and sent men to the Ershi with terms, saying: "If Han does not attack us, we will bring out all good horses for you to take at will and supply Han army food.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan was greatly afraid, ran into the city, held King Wugua's head, and sent men to the Ershi with terms, saying, "If Han does not attack us, we will bring out all good horses for you to take at will and supply Han army food.

sentences.zh: 即不聽我，我盡殺善馬，康居之救又且至，至，我居內，康居居外，與漢軍戰。

translations.literal: If you do not heed us, we will kill all good horses; Kangju's rescue is also about to arrive—when it comes, we will hold the interior and Kangju the exterior, and fight Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not heed us, we will kill all good horses; Kangju's rescue is also about to arrive—when it comes, we will hold the interior and Kangju the exterior, and fight Han troops.

sentences.zh: 孰計之，何從？

translations.literal: Weigh it—which course will you follow?
translations.idiomatic: Weigh it—which course will you follow?

sentences.zh: 」是時，康居候視漢兵尚盛，不敢進。

translations.literal: " At this time Kangju observed Han troops were still strong and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: " At this time Kangju observed Han troops were still strong and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 貳師聞宛城中新得漢人，知穿井，而其內食尚多，計以為「來誅首惡者毋寡，毋寡頭已至，如此不許則堅守，而康居候漢兵罷來救宛，破漢兵必矣」，乃許宛之約。

translations.literal: The Ershi heard that in Dayuan city they had newly obtained Han men who knew how to dig wells, and that food within was still plentiful; he reckoned: "They came to punish the chief culprit Wugua; Wugua's head has arrived—if we do not agree thus they will hold firm, and Kangju will wait until Han troops tire and come to rescue Dayuan; breaking Han troops is certain"—thereupon he agreed to Dayuan's terms.
translations.idiomatic: The Ershi heard that in Dayuan city they had newly obtained Han men who knew how to dig wells, and that food within was still plentiful; he reckoned, "They came to punish the chief culprit Wugua; Wugua's head has arrived—if we do not agree thus they will hold firm, and Kangju will wait until Han troops tire and come to rescue Dayuan; breaking Han troops is certain"—thereupon he agreed to Dayuan's terms.

sentences.zh: 宛乃出其馬，令漢自擇之，而多出食食漢軍。

translations.literal: Dayuan thereupon brought out its horses, let Han choose for themselves, and put out much food to feed Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan thereupon brought out its horses, let Han choose for themselves, and put out much food to feed Han troops.

sentences.zh: 漢軍取其善馬數十匹，中馬以下牝牡三千餘匹，而立宛貴人之故時遇漢善者名昧蔡為宛王，與盟而罷兵。

translations.literal: Han troops took several tens of good horses and over three thousand ordinary horses below that, male and female; they established the Dayuan noble who in former times had treated Han well, named Mei Cai, as King of Dayuan, made covenant, and halted the army.
translations.idiomatic: Han troops took several tens of good horses and over three thousand ordinary horses below that, male and female; they established the Dayuan noble who in former times had treated Han well, named Mei Cai, as King of Dayuan, made covenant, and halted the army.

sentences.zh: 初，貳師起敦煌西，分為數軍，從南、北道。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the Ershi set out west from Dunhuang, he divided into several armies, taking the southern and northern routes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when the Ershi set out west from Dunhuang, he divided into several armies, taking the southern and northern routes.

sentences.zh: 校尉王申生將千餘人別至郁成，郁成王擊滅之，數人脫亡，走貳師。

translations.literal: Colonel Wang Shensheng led over a thousand men separately to Yucheng; the King of Yucheng attacked and destroyed them; several men escaped and fled to the Ershi.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Wang Shensheng led over a thousand men separately to Yucheng; the King of Yucheng attacked and destroyed them; several men escaped and fled to the Ershi.

sentences.zh: 貳師令搜粟都尉上官桀往攻郁成，郁成王亡走康居，桀追至康居。

translations.literal: The Ershi ordered Chief of Grain Search Shangguan Jie to go attack Yucheng; the King of Yucheng fled to Kangju; Jie pursued to Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: The Ershi ordered Chief of Grain Search Shangguan Jie to go attack Yucheng; the King of Yucheng fled to Kangju; Jie pursued to Kangju.

sentences.zh: 康居聞漢已破宛，出郁成王與桀，桀令四騎士縛守詣貳師。

translations.literal: Kangju heard Han had already broken Dayuan, produced the King of Yucheng to Jie; Jie ordered four horsemen to bind and guard him and send him to the Ershi.
translations.idiomatic: Kangju heard Han had already broken Dayuan, produced the King of Yucheng to Jie; Jie ordered four horsemen to bind and guard him and send him to the Ershi.

sentences.zh: 上邽騎士趙弟恐失郁成王，拔劍擊斬其首，追及貳師。

translations.literal: A horseman of Shanggui, Zhao Di, feared losing the King of Yucheng, drew his sword, struck, and beheaded him, and caught up with the Ershi.
translations.idiomatic: A horseman of Shanggui, Zhao Di, feared losing the King of Yucheng, drew his sword, struck, and beheaded him, and caught up with the Ershi.

sentences.zh: 1春，貳師將軍來至京師。

translations.literal: 1 In spring the General of the Ershi came to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring the General of the Ershi came to the capital.

sentences.zh: 貳師所過小國聞宛破，皆使其子弟從入貢獻，見天子，因為質焉。

translations.literal: Small states the Ershi passed heard Dayuan was broken; all sent their sons and younger brothers to follow in tribute and presentation, saw the Son of Heaven, and thereby became hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Small states the Ershi passed heard Dayuan was broken; all sent their sons and younger brothers to follow in tribute and presentation, saw the Son of Heaven, and thereby became hostages.

sentences.zh: 軍還，入馬千餘匹。

translations.literal: When the army returned, they presented over a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, they presented over a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 後行，軍非乏食，戰死不甚多，而將吏貪，不愛卒，侵牟之，以此物故者眾。

translations.literal: On the later march the army did not lack food; battle deaths were not very many; yet generals and officers were greedy, did not cherish the soldiers, and extorted them—for this reason deaths were many.
translations.idiomatic: On the later march the army did not lack food; battle deaths were not very many; yet generals and officers were greedy, did not cherish the soldiers, and extorted them—for this reason deaths were many.

sentences.zh: 天子為萬里而伐，不錄其過，乃下詔封李廣利為海西侯，封趙弟為新畤侯，以上官桀為少府，軍官吏為九卿者三人，諸侯相、郡守、二千石百餘人，千石以下千餘人，奮行者官過其望，以謫過行，皆黜其勞，士卒賜直四萬錢。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, having campaigned for ten thousand li, did not record their faults; he thereupon issued an edict enfeoffing Li Guangli as Marquis of Haixi, enfeoffing Zhao Di as Marquis of Xindi, making Shangguan Jie Privy Treasurer, three army officers and clerks as one of the Nine Ministers, more than a hundred feudal lords' chancellors, commandery governors, and two-thousand-bushel officials, more than a thousand below one thousand bushels; those who strove forward received offices surpassing their hopes, while those who went on account of banishment-faults—all had their merit dismissed; soldiers were given four ten-thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having campaigned ten thousand li, did not record their faults; he issued an edict enfeoffing Li Guangli as Marquis of Haixi and Zhao Di as Marquis of Xindi, making Shangguan Jie Privy Treasurer, three army officers as one of the Nine Ministers, more than a hundred feudal chancellors, commandery governors, and two-thousand-bushel officials, and more than a thousand below that rank; strivers received offices beyond their hopes, while those who went because of banishment-faults had their merit dismissed; soldiers were given forty thousand cash each.

sentences.zh: 匈奴聞貳師征大宛，欲遮之，貳師兵盛，不敢當，即遣騎因樓蘭候漢使後過者，欲絕勿通。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu heard the Eshi army was campaigning against Dayuan and wished to intercept it; the Eshi troops were strong and they dared not confront them, so they immediately sent horsemen by way of Loulan to watch for Han envoys passing afterward, wishing to cut them off and not let them through.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu heard the Eshi army was campaigning against Dayuan and wished to intercept it; the Eshi troops were too strong to confront, so they sent horsemen through Loulan to watch for Han envoys passing afterward, intending to cut them off.

sentences.zh: 時漢軍正任文將兵屯玉門關，捕得生口，知狀以聞。

translations.literal: At this time Han troops under Zheng Ren Wen were garrisoning at Yumen Pass; they captured a living captive, learned the situation, and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Han troops under Zheng Ren Wen were garrisoned at Yumen Pass; they captured a prisoner, learned the situation, and reported it.

sentences.zh: 上詔文便道引兵捕樓蘭王，將詣闕簿責。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wen by the convenient route to lead troops and seize the King of Loulan, to bring him to the palace for register and censure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wen to take the convenient route, lead troops to seize the King of Loulan, and bring him to court for accounting.

sentences.zh: 王對曰：「小國在大國間，不兩屬無以自安，願徙國入居漢地。

translations.literal: The king replied, saying: "A small state between great states—without serving both one cannot secure oneself; your servant wishes to move the state and enter to dwell in Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: The king replied, "A small state between great powers cannot secure itself without serving both; your servant wishes to move the state and settle within Han territory.

sentences.zh: 」上直其言，遣歸國，亦因使候司匈奴，匈奴自是不甚親信樓蘭。

translations.literal: " The emperor considered his words correct, sent him back to his state, and also by this envoy had him spy on the Xiongnu; from this the Xiongnu were not very trusting of Loulan.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his words, sent him back to his state, and also used him to spy on the Xiongnu; from this the Xiongnu no longer trusted Loulan much.

sentences.zh: 自大宛破後，西域震懼，漢使入西域者益得職。

translations.literal: After Dayuan was broken, the Western Regions were shaken with fear; Han envoys entering the Western Regions increasingly obtained their duties.
translations.idiomatic: After Dayuan was defeated, the Western Regions were shaken with fear, and Han envoys in the Western Regions were increasingly able to perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 於是自敦煌西至鹽澤往往起亭，而輪台、渠犁皆有田卒數百人，置使者、校尉領護，以給使外國者。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Dunhuang west to Salt Marsh watchtowers were raised here and there; moreover Luntai and Quli each had several hundred farming soldiers, with envoys and colonels set to lead and guard, to supply those serving foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon from Dunhuang west to Salt Marsh watchtowers were built throughout, and Luntai and Quli each had several hundred farming soldiers, with envoys and colonels appointed to guard and supply those serving foreign states.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，宛貴人以為昧蔡善諛，使我國遇屠，乃相與殺昧蔡，立毋寡昆弟蟬封為宛王，而遣其子入侍於漢。

translations.literal: More than a year later, Dayuan nobles thought Mei Cai was skilled at flattery and had made our state meet slaughter; they thereupon together killed Mei Cai and installed Wugua's younger brother Chanfeng as King of Dayuan, and sent his son to attend at Han.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Dayuan nobles thought Mei Cai was skilled at flattery and had brought slaughter upon their state; they killed Mei Cai and installed Wugua's younger brother Chanfeng as King of Dayuan, and sent his son to attend at Han.

sentences.zh: 漢因使使賂賜，以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Han thereupon sent envoys with bribes and gifts to pacify and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Han thereupon sent envoys with gifts to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 蟬封與漢約，歲獻天馬二匹。

translations.literal: Chanfeng made a pact with Han to present two heavenly horses each year.
translations.idiomatic: Chanfeng agreed with Han to present two heavenly horses each year.

sentences.zh: ----2秋，起明光宮。

translations.literal: ----2 In autumn, the Mingguang Palace was raised.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In autumn the Mingguang Palace was built.

sentences.zh: ----3冬，上行幸回中。

translations.literal: ----3 In winter, the emperor traveled in favor to Huizhong.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In winter the emperor traveled to Huizhong.

sentences.zh: ----4匈奴呴犁湖單于死，匈奴立其弟左大都尉且鞮侯為單于。

translations.literal: ----4 The Xiongnu chanyu Hulu died; the Xiongnu installed his younger brother, the Left Grand Commander Qiedihou, as chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 The Xiongnu chanyu Hulu died; the Xiongnu installed his younger brother, the Left Grand Commander Qiedihou, as chanyu.

sentences.zh: 天子欲因伐宛之威遂困胡，乃下詔曰：「高皇帝遺朕平城之憂，-{高后}-時，單于書絕悖逆。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven wished to take advantage of the prestige of attacking Dayuan to thereupon press the Hu, and issued an edict, saying: "The High Emperor left Us the worry of Pingcheng; in the time of -{Empress Gao}-, the chanyu's letter was utterly rebellious and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to use the prestige of the Dayuan campaign to press the Xiongnu and issued an edict, saying, "The High Emperor left me the worry of Pingcheng; in the time of -{Empress Gao}-, the chanyu's letter was utterly rebellious.

sentences.zh: 昔齊襄公復九世之讎，《春秋》大之。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xiang of Qi avenged a feud of nine generations—the Spring and Autumn Annals praise it.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Xiang of Qi avenged a feud of nine generations—the Spring and Autumn Annals praise it.

sentences.zh: 」且鞮侯單于初立，恐漢襲之，乃曰：「我兒子，安敢望漢天子！

translations.literal: " Chanyu Qiedihou had just been installed and feared Han would strike him; he thereupon said: "I am his son—how would I dare look toward the Han Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: " Chanyu Qiedihou had just been installed and feared a Han attack; he said, "I am his son—how would I dare look toward the Han emperor!

sentences.zh: 漢天子，我丈人行也。

translations.literal: The Han Son of Heaven is my wife's father's senior.
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor is my father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 」因盡歸漢使之不降者路充國等，使使來獻。

translations.literal: " He thereupon completely returned Han envoys who had not submitted, such as Lu Chongguo, and sent envoys to come and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon returned all Han envoys who had not submitted, such as Lu Chongguo, and sent envoys to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，上行幸甘泉，郊泰畤。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled in favor to Sweet Springs and suburban-sacrificed at the Great Altar.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, the emperor traveled to Sweet Springs and performed suburban sacrifice at the Great Altar.

sentences.zh: 三月，行幸河東，祠-{后土}-。

translations.literal: In the third month, he traveled in favor to Hedong and sacrificed to -{Earth Queen}-.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he traveled to Hedong and sacrificed to -{Earth Queen}-.

sentences.zh: ----2上嘉匈奴單于之義，遣中郎將蘇武送匈奴使留在漢者，因厚賂單于，答其善意。

translations.literal: ----2 The emperor praised the Xiongnu chanyu's righteousness and sent Palace Gentleman Su Wu to escort Xiongnu envoys detained in Han, and thereby richly bribed the chanyu to answer his good intent.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 The emperor praised the Xiongnu chanyu's righteousness and sent Palace Gentleman Su Wu to escort Xiongnu envoys detained in Han, richly bribing the chanyu to answer his good intent.

sentences.zh: 武與副中郎將張勝與假吏常惠等俱。

translations.literal: Wu together with Deputy Palace Gentleman Zhang Sheng and acting clerk Chang Hui and others went.
translations.idiomatic: Wu went together with Deputy Palace Gentleman Zhang Sheng and acting clerk Chang Hui and others.

sentences.zh: 既至匈奴，置幣遣單于。

translations.literal: Having reached the Xiongnu, they set out gifts and sent them to the chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Having reached the Xiongnu, they presented gifts to the chanyu.

sentences.zh: 單于益驕，非漢所望也。

translations.literal: The chanyu grew increasingly arrogant—not what Han had hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu grew increasingly arrogant—not what Han had hoped for.

sentences.zh: 會緱王與長水虞常等及衛律所將降者，陰相與謀劫單于母閼氏歸漢。

translations.literal: It happened that the Gou king, Changshui Yu Chang and others, and those who had surrendered led by Wei Lü secretly together plotted to seize the chanyu's mother the yanzhi and return to Han.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Gou king, Changshui Yu Chang and others, and the surrenderers led by Wei Lü secretly plotted together to seize the chanyu's mother the yanzhi and return to Han.

sentences.zh: 衛律者，父故長水胡人，律善協律都尉李延年，延年薦言律使於匈奴，使還，聞延年家收，遂亡降匈奴。

translations.literal: Wei Lü—his father was formerly a Changshui Hu man; Lü was skilled with Director of Harmonizing the Pitch Pipes Li Yanian; Yanian recommended saying Lü should be sent to the Xiongnu; when the mission returned he heard Yanian's household was seized and thereupon fled and surrendered to the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lü—his father was formerly a Changshui Hu man; Lü was on good terms with Director of Harmonizing the Pitch Pipes Li Yanian; Yanian recommended that Lü be sent to the Xiongnu; when the mission returned he heard Yanian's household had been seized and fled to surrender to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 單于愛之，與謀國事，立為丁靈王。

translations.literal: The chanyu favored him, deliberated state affairs with him, and installed him as King of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu favored him, deliberated state affairs with him, and made him King of Dingling.

sentences.zh: 虞常在漢時素與副張勝相知，私候勝曰：「聞漢天子甚怨衛律，常能為漢伏弩射殺之。

translations.literal: Yu Chang in Han times had long known Deputy Zhang Sheng; he privately waited on Sheng and said: "I have heard the Han Son of Heaven greatly hates Wei Lü; Chang can for Han lie in ambush with crossbow and shoot and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chang in Han times had long known Deputy Zhang Sheng; he privately approached Sheng and said, "I have heard the Han emperor greatly hates Wei Lü; Chang can lie in ambush for Han with a crossbow and kill him.

sentences.zh: 吾母、弟在漢，幸蒙其賞賜。

translations.literal: My mother and younger brother are in Han; I hope to receive their rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: My mother and younger brother are in Han; I hope to receive their rewards.

sentences.zh: 」張勝許之，以貨物與常。

translations.literal: " Zhang Sheng promised him and gave goods to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Sheng promised him and gave goods to Chang.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，單于出獵，獨閼氏、子弟在，虞常等七十餘人欲發，其一人夜亡告之。

translations.literal: More than a month later the chanyu went out hunting; only the yanzhi and sons and younger brothers remained; Yu Chang and more than seventy men wished to rise, but one man fled by night and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later the chanyu went hunting; only the yanzhi and his sons and younger brothers remained; Yu Chang and more than seventy men wished to act, but one man fled by night and reported it.

sentences.zh: 單于子弟發兵與戰，緱王等皆死，虞常生得。

translations.literal: The chanyu's sons and younger brothers raised troops and fought; the Gou king and others all died; Yu Chang was taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu's sons and younger brothers raised troops and fought; the Gou king and others all died; Yu Chang was captured alive.

sentences.zh: 單于使衛律治其事。

translations.literal: The chanyu had Wei Lü handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu had Wei Lü handle the matter.

sentences.zh: 張勝聞之，恐前語發，以狀語武。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng heard of it, feared their earlier words would be exposed, and told Wu the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng heard of it, feared their earlier words would be exposed, and told Wu the situation.

sentences.zh: 武曰：「事如此，此必及我，見犯乃死，重負國。

translations.literal: Wu said: "The affair being like this, this will surely reach me; to be violated and then die heavily burdens the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, "The affair being like this, this will surely reach me; to be violated and then die would heavily burden the state.

sentences.zh: 」欲自殺。

translations.literal: " He wished to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He wished to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 勝、惠共止之。

translations.literal: Sheng and Hui together stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Hui together stopped him.

sentences.zh: 虞常果引張勝。

translations.literal: Yu Chang indeed implicated Zhang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chang indeed implicated Zhang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 單于怒，召諸貴人議，欲殺漢使者。

translations.literal: The chanyu was enraged, summoned the various nobles to deliberate, and wished to kill the Han envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu was enraged, summoned the nobles to deliberate, and wished to kill the Han envoys.

sentences.zh: 左伊秩訾曰：「即謀單于，何以復加！

translations.literal: Left Yizhi Ze said: "If they already plotted against the chanyu, how can one add more!
translations.idiomatic: Left Yizhi Ze said, "If they already plotted against the chanyu, how can one add more!

sentences.zh: 宜皆降之。

translations.literal: They should all be made to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They should all be made to surrender.

sentences.zh: 」單于使衛律召武受辭。

translations.literal: " The chanyu had Wei Lü summon Wu to receive his confession.
translations.idiomatic: " The chanyu had Wei Lü summon Wu to take his confession.

sentences.zh: 武謂惠等：「屈節辱命，雖生，何面目以歸漢！

translations.literal: Wu said to Hui and the others: "To bend one's integrity and disgrace one's commission—even living, with what face could one return to Han!
translations.idiomatic: Wu said to Hui and the others, "To bend one's integrity and disgrace one's commission—even living, with what face could one return to Han!

sentences.zh: 」引佩刀自刺。

translations.literal: " He drew his girdle knife and stabbed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He drew his girdle knife and stabbed himself.

sentences.zh: 衛律驚，自抱持武，馳召醫，鑿地為坎，置熅火，覆武其上，蹈其背以出血。

translations.literal: Wei Lü was startled, himself embraced and held Wu, galloped to summon a physician, dug the ground into a pit, set smoldering fire, covered Wu above it, and trod his back to draw out blood.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lü was startled, himself embraced Wu, galloped to summon a physician, dug a pit in the ground, set smoldering fire, covered Wu with it, and trod his back to draw out blood.

sentences.zh: 武氣絕，半日復息。

translations.literal: Wu's breath was cut off; after half a day he breathed again.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's breath stopped; after half a day he breathed again.

sentences.zh: 惠等哭，輿歸營。

translations.literal: Hui and the others wept and carried him back to camp in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and the others wept and carried him back to camp in a litter.

sentences.zh: 單于壯其節，朝夕遣人候問武，而收系張勝。

translations.literal: The chanyu admired his integrity, morning and evening sent men to inquire after Wu, and detained Zhang Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu admired his integrity, sent men morning and evening to inquire after Wu, and detained Zhang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 武益愈，單于使使曉武，欲降之，會論虞常，欲因此時降武；

translations.literal: Wu grew increasingly recovered; the chanyu sent envoys to enlighten Wu, wishing to make him surrender; it happened they judged Yu Chang, wishing thereby to make Wu surrender at this time;
translations.idiomatic: As Wu recovered, the chanyu sent envoys to persuade Wu to surrender; it happened they judged Yu Chang, wishing thereby to make Wu surrender at that moment;

sentences.zh: 劍斬虞常已，律曰：「漢使張勝謀殺單于近臣，當死，單于募降者赦罪。

translations.literal: having already beheaded Yu Chang with the sword, Lü said: "Han envoy Zhang Sheng plotted to kill the chanyu's close minister—he should die; the chanyu recruits surrenderers and pardons crime.
translations.idiomatic: having beheaded Yu Chang with the sword, Lü said, "Han envoy Zhang Sheng plotted to kill the chanyu's close minister—he should die; the chanyu recruits surrenderers and pardons crime.

sentences.zh: 」舉劍欲擊之，勝請降。

translations.literal: " He raised the sword wishing to strike him; Sheng requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " He raised the sword to strike him; Sheng asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 律謂武曰：「副有罪，當相坐。

translations.literal: Lü said to Wu: "The deputy has crime; you should share punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Lü said to Wu, "The deputy is guilty; you should share punishment.

sentences.zh: 」武曰：「本無謀，又非親屬，何謂相坐！

translations.literal: " Wu said: "Originally there was no plotting, and moreover we are not kin—what is meant by sharing punishment!
translations.idiomatic: " Wu said, "Originally there was no plotting, and moreover we are not kin—what is meant by sharing punishment!

sentences.zh: 」復舉劍擬之，武不動。

translations.literal: " He again raised the sword and gestured at him; Wu did not move.
translations.idiomatic: " He again raised the sword and gestured at him; Wu did not move.

sentences.zh: 律曰：「蘇君，律前負漢歸匈奴，幸蒙大恩賜號稱王，擁眾數萬，馬畜彌山，富貴如此！

translations.literal: Lü said: "Master Su—Lü formerly turned his back on Han and returned to the Xiongnu; fortunately I received great favor, was granted a title and styled king, hold masses of several tens of thousands, horses and livestock fill the mountains—wealth and honor like this!
translations.idiomatic: Lü said, "Master Su—Lü formerly turned his back on Han and returned to the Xiongnu; fortunately I received great favor, was granted a title and styled king, hold masses of tens of thousands, horses and livestock fill the mountains—wealth and honor like this!

sentences.zh: 蘇君今日降，明日復然；

translations.literal: Master Su, if you surrender today, tomorrow will be the same again;
translations.idiomatic: Master Su, if you surrender today, tomorrow will be the same again;

sentences.zh: 空以身膏草野，誰復知之！

translations.literal: in vain you would make your body grease the wild grass—who would know you again!
translations.idiomatic: in vain you would make your body grease the wild grass—who would know you again!

sentences.zh: 」武不應。

translations.literal: " Wu did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: " Wu did not respond.

sentences.zh: 律曰：「君因我降，與君為兄弟；

translations.literal: Lü said: "If you surrender through me, I will be brothers with you;
translations.idiomatic: Lü said, "If you surrender through me, I will be brothers with you;

sentences.zh: 今不聽吾計，後雖欲復見我，尚可得乎！

translations.literal: now if you do not heed my plan, later even if you wish again to see me, can you still obtain it!
translations.idiomatic: now if you do not heed my plan, later even if you wish again to see me, can you still obtain it!

sentences.zh: 」武罵律曰：「汝為人臣子，不顧恩義，畔主背親，為降虜於蠻夷，何以汝為見！

translations.literal: " Wu cursed Lü, saying: "You are a man's minister and son, yet do not think of grace and righteousness, turn your back on your lord and abandon your kin, become a surrendering captive among barbarians—why should I see you!
translations.idiomatic: " Wu cursed Lü, saying, "You are a man's minister and son, yet do not think of grace and righteousness, turn your back on your lord and abandon your kin, become a surrendering captive among barbarians—why should I see you!

sentences.zh: 且單于信汝，使決人死生，不平心持正，反欲鬥兩主，觀禍敗。

translations.literal: Moreover the chanyu trusts you and has you decide men's life and death; you do not hold your heart level and straight, yet wish instead to set the two lords fighting and watch disaster and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the chanyu trusts you and has you decide men's life and death; you do not hold your heart level and straight, yet wish instead to set the two rulers fighting and watch disaster and defeat.

sentences.zh: 南越殺漢使者，屠為九郡；

translations.literal: Nanyue killed Han envoys and was slaughtered into nine commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: Nanyue killed Han envoys and was slaughtered into nine commanderies;

sentences.zh: 宛王殺漢使者，頭懸北闕；

translations.literal: the King of Dayuan killed Han envoys and his head hung at the northern gate;
translations.idiomatic: the King of Dayuan killed Han envoys and his head hung at the northern gate;

sentences.zh: 朝鮮殺漢使者，即時誅滅；

translations.literal: Chaoxian killed Han envoys and was immediately exterminated;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxian killed Han envoys and was immediately exterminated;

sentences.zh: 獨匈奴未耳。

translations.literal: only the Xiongnu have not yet.
translations.idiomatic: only the Xiongnu have not yet.

sentences.zh: 若知我不降明，欲令兩國相攻，匈奴之禍從我始矣。

translations.literal: If you know clearly that I will not surrender, you wish to make the two states attack each other—the Xiongnu's disaster will begin with me.
translations.idiomatic: If you know clearly that I will not surrender, you wish to make the two states attack each other—the Xiongnu's disaster will begin with me.

sentences.zh: 」律知武終不可脅，白單于，單于愈益欲降之。

translations.literal: " Lü knew Wu in the end could not be coerced, reported to the chanyu, and the chanyu increasingly wished to make him surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü knew Wu in the end could not be coerced, reported to the chanyu, and the chanyu increasingly wished to make him surrender.

sentences.zh: 乃幽武置大窖中，絕不飲食；

translations.literal: He thereupon imprisoned Wu and placed him in a great cellar, cutting off all drink and food;
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Wu in a great cellar and cut off all drink and food;

sentences.zh: 天雨雪，武臥，嚙雪與旃毛並咽之，數日不死。

translations.literal: Heaven snowed rain; Wu lay down, chewed snow together with felt fur and swallowed it, and several days did not die.
translations.idiomatic: It snowed; Wu lay down, chewed snow together with felt fur and swallowed it, and did not die for several days.

sentences.zh: 匈奴以為神，乃徙武北海上無人處，使牧羝，曰：「羝乳乃得歸。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu thought him divine; he thereupon moved Wu to the northern sea frontier where no men were, had him herd rams, and said: "When the rams give milk you may return.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu thought him divine; they moved Wu to the northern sea frontier where no men were, had him herd rams, and said, "When the rams give milk you may return.

sentences.zh: 」別其官屬常惠等，各置他所。

translations.literal: " He separated his attendant officials Chang Hui and others, each placed in another place.
translations.idiomatic: " They separated his attendants Chang Hui and others, each placed elsewhere.

sentences.zh: ----3天雨白牦。

translations.literal: ----3 Heaven rained white yak.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Heaven rained white yak.

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, great drought.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer there was great drought.

sentences.zh: ----5五月，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----5 In the fifth month, an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In the fifth month there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----6發謫戍屯五原。

translations.literal: ----6 Conscripted banishment-garrison troops were sent to garrison Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Banishment-garrison troops were sent to garrison Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: ----7浞野侯趙破奴自匈奴亡歸。

translations.literal: ----7 Marquis of Zhuoye Zhao Ponu fled from the Xiongnu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 Marquis of Zhuoye Zhao Ponu fled from the Xiongnu and returned.

sentences.zh: ----8是歲，濟南太守王卿為御史大夫。

translations.literal: ----8 This year, Jinan Administrator Wang Qing became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 This year Jinan Administrator Wang Qing became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 1春，上行幸東海。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the emperor traveled in favor to the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring the emperor traveled to the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 還，幸回中。

translations.literal: Returning, he favored Huizhong.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he traveled to Huizhong.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，五月，遣貳師將軍廣利以三萬騎出酒泉，擊右賢王於天山，得胡首虜萬餘級而還。

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fifth month, Eshi General Guangli was sent with thirty thousand horsemen out from Jiuquan to strike the Right Worthy King at Heavenly Mountain, obtaining more than ten thousand Hu heads and captives and returning.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fifth month, Eshi General Guangli was sent with thirty thousand horsemen from Jiuquan to strike the Right Worthy King at Heavenly Mountain, taking more than ten thousand Xiongnu heads and captives and returning.

sentences.zh: 匈奴大圍貳師將軍，漢軍乏食數日，死傷者多。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu greatly besieged the Eshi general; Han troops lacked food for several days and many died or were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu greatly besieged the Eshi general; Han troops lacked food for several days and many died or were wounded.

sentences.zh: 假司馬隴西趙充國與士百餘人潰圍陷陳，貳師引兵隨之，遂得解。

translations.literal: Acting Major Longxi Zhao Chongguo with more than a hundred soldiers broke the encirclement and charged the formation; the Eshi general led troops following them and thereupon obtained relief.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Major Longxi Zhao Chongguo with more than a hundred soldiers broke the encirclement and charged the formation; the Eshi general led troops after them and was thereby relieved.

sentences.zh: 漢兵物故什六七，充國身被二十餘創。

translations.literal: Han troops perished seven or eight in ten; Chongguo himself received more than twenty wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Han troops lost seven or eight in ten; Chongguo himself received more than twenty wounds.

sentences.zh: 貳師奏狀，詔征充國詣行在所，帝親見，視其創，嗟歎之，拜為中郎。

translations.literal: The Eshi general memorialized the situation; an edict summoned Chongguo to the traveling palace; the emperor personally saw him, looked at his wounds, sighed and praised him, and appointed him Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The Eshi general memorialized the situation; an edict summoned Chongguo to the traveling palace; the emperor personally saw him, looked at his wounds, sighed and praised him, and appointed him Palace Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 漢復使因杅將軍敖出西河，與強弩都尉路博德會涿塗山，無所得。

translations.literal: Han again sent Yinya General Ao out from Xihe to meet Strong Crossbow Colonel Lu Bode at Zhuotu Mountain—nothing obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Han again sent Yinya General Ao out from Xihe to meet Strong Crossbow Colonel Lu Bode at Zhuotu Mountain and obtained nothing.

sentences.zh: 初，李廣有孫陵，為侍中，善騎射，愛人下士。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Guang had a grandson Ling, who was Palace Attendant, skilled at mounted archery, and loved men and humbled himself before scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Li Guang had a grandson Ling, who was Palace Attendant, skilled at mounted archery, and loved men and humbled himself before scholars.

sentences.zh: 帝以為有廣之風，拜騎都尉，使將丹陽、楚人五千人，教射酒泉、張掖以備胡。

translations.literal: The emperor thought he had Guang's manner, appointed him Cavalry Commandant, and had him lead five thousand men of Danyang and Chu, teaching archery at Jiuquan and Zhangye to prepare against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought he had Guang's manner, appointed him Cavalry Commandant, and had him lead five thousand men of Danyang and Chu to teach archery at Jiuquan and Zhangye against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 及貳師擊匈奴，上詔陵，欲使為貳師將輜重，陵叩頭自請曰：「臣所將屯邊者，皆荊楚勇士奇材劍客也，力扼虎，射命中，願得自當一隊，到-{蘭于}-山南以分單于兵，毋令專向貳師軍。

translations.literal: When the Eshi army struck the Xiongnu, the emperor ordered Ling, wishing to have him for the Eshi general lead baggage trains; Ling knocked his head and requested himself, saying: "Those your servant leads garrisoning the border are all Jing-Chu warriors of strange talent and sword guests—strength to throttle tigers, shooting that hits the mark; your servant wishes to take a separate command, reach south of -{Lan Yu}- Mountain to divide the chanyu's troops, and not let them focus solely on the Eshi army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eshi army struck the Xiongnu, the emperor ordered Ling, wishing to have him lead baggage trains for the Eshi general; Ling knocked his head and requested himself, saying, "Those your servant leads garrisoning the border are all Jing-Chu warriors of strange talent and swordsmen—strength to throttle tigers, shooting that hits the mark; your servant wishes to take a separate command, reach south of -{Lan Yu}- Mountain to divide the chanyu's troops, and not let them focus solely on the Eshi army.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「將惡相屬邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Do generals dislike being subordinate to one another!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Do generals dislike being subordinate to one another!

sentences.zh: 吾發軍多，無騎予女。

translations.literal: I am sending out many armies and have no cavalry to give you.
translations.idiomatic: I am sending out many armies and have no cavalry to give you.

sentences.zh: 」陵對：「無所事騎，臣願以少擊眾，步兵五千人涉單于庭。

translations.literal: " Ling replied: "Without needing cavalry, your servant wishes with few to strike many—five thousand foot soldiers crossing the chanyu's court.
translations.idiomatic: " Ling replied, "Without needing cavalry, your servant wishes with few to strike many—five thousand foot soldiers crossing the chanyu's court.

sentences.zh: 」上壯而許之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was impressed and assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was impressed and assented.

sentences.zh: 因詔路博德將兵半道迎陵軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Lu Bode to lead troops halfway to meet Ling's army.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered Lu Bode to lead troops halfway to meet Ling's army.

sentences.zh: 博德亦羞為陵後距，奏言：「方秋，匈奴馬肥，未可與戰，願留陵至春俱出。

translations.literal: Bode also was ashamed to be Ling's rear support and memorialized, saying: "It is just autumn; Xiongnu horses are fat and one cannot yet fight them; your servant wishes to keep Ling until spring and go out together.
translations.idiomatic: Bode was also ashamed to be Ling's rear support and memorialized, saying, "It is just autumn; Xiongnu horses are fat and one cannot yet fight them; your servant wishes to keep Ling until spring and go out together.

sentences.zh: 」上怒，疑陵悔不欲出而教博德上書，乃詔博德引兵擊匈奴於西河。

translations.literal: " The emperor was enraged, suspected Ling regretted and did not wish to go out and had taught Bode to memorialize, and thereupon ordered Bode to lead troops and strike the Xiongnu in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was enraged, suspected Ling regretted going out and had coached Bode to memorialize, and ordered Bode to lead troops and strike the Xiongnu in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 詔陵以九月發，出遮虜障，至東浚稽山南龍勒水上，徘徊觀虜，即亡所見，還，抵受降城休士。

translations.literal: He ordered Ling to set out in the ninth month, go out through the barrier that blocks the barbarians, reach south of Eastern Junji Mountain at Dragon Rein River, linger and observe the barbarians—immediately nothing was seen—and return, reaching Surrender-Receiving City to rest the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Ling to set out in the ninth month, go out through the barbarian-blocking barrier to south of Eastern Junji Mountain at Dragon Rein River, linger to observe the barbarians—seeing nothing—and return to Surrender-Receiving City to rest his troops.

sentences.zh: 陵於是將其步卒五千人，出居延，北行三十日，至浚稽山止營，舉圖所過山川地形，使麾下騎陳步樂還以聞。

translations.literal: Ling thereupon led his five thousand foot soldiers, went out from Juyan, marched north thirty days, reached Junji Mountain and halted camp, raised a map of the mountains and rivers and terrain passed through, and sent his subordinate cavalryman Chen Bule back to report.
translations.idiomatic: Ling thereupon led his five thousand foot soldiers out from Juyan, marched north thirty days to Junji Mountain and halted camp, mapped the mountains, rivers, and terrain passed through, and sent his subordinate cavalryman Chen Bule back to report.

sentences.zh: 步樂召見，道陵將率得士死力，上甚悅，拜步樂為郎。

translations.literal: Bule was summoned to audience; he spoke of how Ling as general obtained soldiers' death-strength; the emperor was very pleased and appointed Bule as Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bule was summoned to audience; he reported that Ling as general won his men's utmost loyalty; the emperor was very pleased and appointed Bule Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 陵至浚稽山，與單于相值，騎可三萬圍陵軍，軍居兩山間，以大車為營。

translations.literal: Ling reached Junji Mountain and met the chanyu head-on; horsemen numbering perhaps thirty thousand surrounded Ling's army; the army dwelt between two mountains, using great carts as camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ling reached Junji Mountain and met the chanyu head-on; perhaps thirty thousand horsemen surrounded Ling's army, which camped between two mountains using great carts as fortification.

sentences.zh: 陵引士出營外為陳，前行持戟、盾，後行持弓、弩。

translations.literal: Ling led soldiers out beyond the camp to form a battle array: the front rank held halberds and shields, the rear rank held bows and crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Ling led his men out beyond the camp to form a battle line: the front rank held halberds and shields, the rear rank bows and crossbows.

sentences.zh: 虜見漢軍少，直前就營。

translations.literal: The barbarians saw the Han army was few and went straight forward to the camp.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians saw the Han force was small and charged straight at the camp.

sentences.zh: 陵搏戰攻之，千弩俱發，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Ling fought hand to hand and struck them; a thousand crossbows fired together and they fell as the bowstrings answered.
translations.idiomatic: Ling fought hand to hand and struck them; a thousand crossbows fired together and the enemy fell as the strings sounded.

sentences.zh: 虜還走上山，漢軍追擊殺數千人。

translations.literal: The barbarians turned back and ran up the mountain; the Han army pursued and killed several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians retreated up the mountain; the Han army pursued and killed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 單于大驚，召左、右地兵八萬餘騎攻陵。

translations.literal: The chanyu was greatly startled and summoned left and right territorial troops—more than eighty thousand horsemen—to attack Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu was greatly startled and summoned left and right territorial troops—more than eighty thousand horsemen—to attack Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵且戰且引南行，數日，抵山谷中，連戰，士卒中矢傷，三創者載輦。

translations.literal: Ling fought while withdrawing south; after several days he reached a mountain valley; in continuous fighting soldiers were struck by arrows and wounded—those with three wounds were carried in litters.
translations.idiomatic: Ling fought while withdrawing south; after several days he reached a mountain valley; in continuous fighting his men were wounded by arrows—those with three wounds were carried in litters.

sentences.zh: 兩創者將車，一創者持兵戰，復斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: Those with two wounds drove the carts; those with one wound held weapons and fought; they again beheaded more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Those with two wounds drove the carts; those with one wound fought with weapons in hand; they again took more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 引兵東南，循故龍城道行四五日，抵大澤葭葦中，虜從上風縱火，陵亦令軍中縱火以自救。

translations.literal: He led the army southeast, following the old Dragon City road for four or five days, reaching a great marsh of reeds; the barbarians set fire from upwind, and Ling also ordered the army to set fire to save themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army southeast along the old Dragon City road for four or five days to a great marsh of reeds; the barbarians set fire from upwind, and Ling also ordered his men to set fire to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 南行至山下，單于在南山上，使其子將騎擊陵。

translations.literal: Marching south to below the mountain, the chanyu was on the southern mountain and sent his son to lead horsemen and strike Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Marching south to the foot of the mountain, the chanyu was on the southern slope and sent his son to lead horsemen against Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵軍步鬥樹木間，復殺數千人，因發連弩射單于，單于下走。

translations.literal: Ling's army fought on foot among the trees, again killing several thousand; they thereupon loosed repeating crossbows to shoot the chanyu, and the chanyu ran down.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's army fought on foot among the trees and again killed several thousand; they then loosed repeating crossbows at the chanyu, and the chanyu fled downhill.

sentences.zh: 是日捕得虜，言「單于曰：『此漢精兵，擊之不能下，日夜引吾南近塞，得無有伏兵乎？

translations.literal: That day they captured a barbarian who said: "The chanyu said: 'These are Han elite troops; striking them we cannot take them down; day and night they draw me south near the passes—is there perhaps an ambush?
translations.idiomatic: That day they captured a barbarian who said, "The chanyu said, 'These are Han elite troops; we cannot bring them down; day and night they draw me south near the passes—is there perhaps an ambush?

sentences.zh: 』諸當戶君長皆言：『單于自將數萬騎擊漢數千人不能滅，後無以復使邊臣，令漢益輕匈奴。

translations.literal: ' The various household chieftains all said: 'The chanyu himself leading tens of thousands of horsemen could not destroy several thousand Han; afterward there will be no way to send border ministers again—this will make Han increasingly look down on the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: ' The various household chieftains all said, 'The chanyu himself leading tens of thousands of horsemen could not destroy several thousand Han; afterward there will be no way to use border ministers again—Han will look down on the Xiongnu all the more.

sentences.zh: 復力戰山谷間，尚四五十里，得平地，不能破，乃還。

translations.literal: Fight again in the mountain valleys; still forty or fifty li to level ground; if we cannot break them, then return.
translations.idiomatic: Fight again in the mountain valleys; still forty or fifty li to level ground; if we cannot break them, then return.

sentences.zh: 是時陵軍益急，匈奴騎多，戰一日數十合，復傷殺虜二千餘人。

translations.literal: At this time Ling's army grew increasingly pressed; Xiongnu horsemen were many; in one day they fought several tens of engagements and again wounded and killed more than two thousand barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Ling's army grew increasingly pressed; Xiongnu horsemen were many; in one day they fought dozens of engagements and again wounded and killed more than two thousand barbarians.

sentences.zh: 虜不利，欲去，會陵軍候管敢為校尉所辱，亡降匈奴，具言：「陵軍無後救，射矢且盡，獨將軍麾下及校尉成安侯韓延年各八百人為前行，以黃與白為幟。

translations.literal: The barbarians were disadvantaged and wished to leave; it happened that Ling's army scout Guan Gan had been insulted by a colonel, fled and surrendered to the Xiongnu, and fully stated: "Ling's army has no rear relief; shooting arrows are nearly exhausted; only the general's personal followers and Colonel Marquis of Cheng'an Han Yannian, eight hundred each, are the forward rank, using yellow and white as banners.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians were at a disadvantage and wished to withdraw; it happened that Ling's army scout Guan Gan had been insulted by a colonel, fled and surrendered to the Xiongnu, and fully reported, "Ling's army has no rear relief; arrows are nearly spent; only the general's personal followers and Colonel Marquis of Cheng'an Han Yannian, eight hundred men each, form the forward rank, with yellow and white as their banners.

sentences.zh: 當使精騎射之，即破矣。

translations.literal: One should send elite horsemen to shoot them—then they will be broken at once.
translations.idiomatic: Send elite horsemen to shoot them and they will be broken at once.

sentences.zh: 」單于得敢大喜，使騎並攻漢軍，疾呼曰：「李陵、韓延年趣降！

translations.literal: " The chanyu, obtaining Gan, was greatly pleased, sent horsemen together to attack the Han army, and urgently shouted: "Li Ling and Han Yannian—hurry and surrender!
translations.idiomatic: " The chanyu, obtaining Gan, was greatly pleased, sent horsemen together to attack the Han army, and urgently shouted, "Li Ling and Han Yannian—hurry and surrender!

sentences.zh: 」遂遮道急攻陵。

translations.literal: " He thereupon blocked the road and urgently attacked Ling.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon blocked the road and urgently attacked Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵居谷中，虜在山上，四面射，矢如雨下。

translations.literal: Ling dwelt in the valley; the barbarians were on the mountain; they shot from four sides and arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was in the valley while the barbarians were on the mountain; they shot from four sides and arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 漢軍南行，未至鞮汗山，一日五十萬矢皆盡，即棄車去。

translations.literal: The Han army marched south; before reaching Dihan Mountain, in one day five hundred thousand arrows were all exhausted; they immediately abandoned the carts and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Han army marched south; before reaching Dihan Mountain, in one day five hundred thousand arrows were all spent; they immediately abandoned the carts.

sentences.zh: 士尚三千餘人，徒斬車輻而持之，軍吏持尺刀，抵山，入狹谷，單于遮其後，乘隅下壘石，士卒多死，不得行。

translations.literal: Soldiers still numbered more than three thousand; they only chopped cart wheel hubs to hold, army officers held foot-long knives; reaching the mountain they entered a narrow valley; the chanyu blocked their rear; from corners above they rolled down piled stones; soldiers mostly died and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand soldiers remained; they chopped cart wheel hubs to wield as weapons, officers held foot-long knives; reaching the mountain they entered a narrow valley; the chanyu blocked their rear; from the heights they rolled down piled stones; many soldiers died and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 昏後，陵便衣獨步出營，止左右：「毋隨，丈夫一取單于耳！

translations.literal: After dusk, Ling changed clothes and walked alone out of camp, stopping his attendants: "Do not follow; a man should once take the chanyu's ear!
translations.idiomatic: After dusk Ling changed clothes and walked alone out of camp, stopping his attendants: "Do not follow—a man should once take the chanyu's ear!

sentences.zh: 」良久，陵還，太息曰：「兵敗，死矣！

translations.literal: " After a long while Ling returned, sighed deeply, and said: "The army is defeated—I am as good as dead!
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while Ling returned, sighed deeply, and said, "The army is defeated—I am as good as dead!

sentences.zh: 」於是盡斬旌旗，及珍寶埋地中，陵歎曰：「復得數十矢，足以脫矣。

translations.literal: " He thereupon completely cut down the banners and flags and buried treasures in the ground; Ling sighed and said: "If I could again obtain several tens of arrows, it would be enough to escape.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon cut down all banners and flags and buried treasures in the ground; Ling sighed and said, "If I could obtain even several tens of arrows more, it would be enough to escape.

sentences.zh: 今無兵復戰，天明，坐受縛矣。

translations.literal: Now without weapons to fight again, at daybreak I will sit and accept binding.
translations.idiomatic: Now without weapons to fight again, at daybreak I will sit and accept binding.

sentences.zh: 各鳥獸散，猶有得脫歸報天子者。

translations.literal: Each like birds and beasts scatter—there may still be some who escape and return to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Each scatter like birds and beasts—some may still escape and return to report to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」令軍士人持二升糒，一片冰，期至遮障者相待。

translations.literal: " He ordered the soldiers each to take two sheng of dry provisions and one piece of ice, fixing a time to meet at the blocking barrier.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered each soldier to take two sheng of dry provisions and one piece of ice, fixing a time to meet at the blocking barrier.

sentences.zh: 夜半時，擊鼓起士，鼓不鳴。

translations.literal: At midnight he beat the drum to rouse the soldiers; the drum did not sound.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he beat the drum to rouse the soldiers; the drum did not sound.

sentences.zh: 陵與韓延年俱上馬，壯士從者十餘人，虜騎數千追之，韓延年戰死。

translations.literal: Ling and Han Yannian both mounted horses; stalwart followers numbered more than ten; several thousand barbarian horsemen pursued them; Han Yannian died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Ling and Han Yannian both mounted; more than ten stalwarts followed; several thousand barbarian horsemen pursued them; Han Yannian died fighting.

sentences.zh: 陵曰：「無面目報陛下！

translations.literal: Ling said: "I have no face to report to Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Ling said, "I have no face to report to Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 」遂降。

translations.literal: " He thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon surrendered.

sentences.zh: 軍人分散，脫至塞者四百餘人。

translations.literal: The soldiers scattered; those who escaped to the passes numbered more than four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers scattered; more than four hundred escaped to the passes.

sentences.zh: 陵敗處去塞百餘里，邊塞以聞。

translations.literal: The place where Ling was defeated was more than a hundred li from the passes; the border passes reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The place where Ling was defeated was more than a hundred li from the passes; the border reported it.

sentences.zh: 上欲陵死戰；

translations.literal: The emperor wished Ling to fight to the death;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished Ling to fight to the death;

sentences.zh: 後聞陵降，上怒甚，責問陳步樂，步樂自殺。

translations.literal: later hearing Ling had surrendered, the emperor was greatly enraged, censured and questioned Chen Bule, and Bule killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: later hearing Ling had surrendered, the emperor was greatly enraged, censured Chen Bule, and Bule killed himself.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆罪陵，上以問太史令司馬遷，遷盛言：「陵事親孝，與士信，常奮不顧身以徇國家之急，其素所畜積也，有國士之風。

translations.literal: The host of ministers all blamed Ling; the emperor questioned Grand Astrologer Sima Qian; Qian strongly stated: "Ling served his parents with filial piety, was faithful with soldiers, and constantly strove without regard for his body to follow the state's urgent needs—what he had long stored up; he had the manner of a state's scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all blamed Ling; the emperor questioned Grand Astrologer Sima Qian; Qian strongly argued, "Ling served his parents filially, was faithful to his men, and constantly strove without regard for his body in the state's urgent need—what he had long cultivated; he had the manner of a state's finest man.

sentences.zh: 今舉事一不幸，全軀保妻子之臣隨而媒糵其短，誠可痛也！

translations.literal: Now in one undertaking he met misfortune, yet ministers who preserve their bodies and protect wife and children follow to slander and magnify his faults—truly this is painful!
translations.idiomatic: Now in one misfortune, ministers who preserve their bodies and protect wife and children follow to slander and magnify his faults—truly this is painful!

sentences.zh: 且陵提步卒不滿五千，深蹂戎馬之地，抑數萬之師，虜救死扶傷不暇，悉舉引弓之民共攻圍之，轉鬥千里，矢盡道窮，士張空弮，冒白刃，北首爭死敵，得人之死力，雖古名將不過也。

translations.literal: Moreover Ling led foot soldiers not reaching five thousand, deeply trampled the land of barbarian horses, suppressed an army of tens of thousands; the barbarians had no leisure for rescuing the wounded and tending the hurt; they completely raised bow-drawing peoples together to attack and besiege him; he turned and fought a thousand li; arrows exhausted and the road ended; soldiers drew empty bowstocks, braved white blades, faced north striving to die against the enemy, obtaining men's death-strength—even ancient famed generals did not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ling led fewer than five thousand foot soldiers, deeply invaded barbarian horse country, and held down an army of tens of thousands; the barbarians had no leisure to tend their wounded; they raised all their bowmen to attack and besiege him; he fought turning battle over a thousand li; arrows spent and the road ended; his men drew empty bowstocks, braved naked blades, faced north striving to die against the enemy, and won men's utmost loyalty—even ancient famed generals did not surpass this.

sentences.zh: 身雖陷敗，然其所摧敗亦足暴於天下。

translations.literal: Though his person fell into defeat, yet what he crushed and defeated was also sufficient to be displayed to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was defeated, what he crushed and defeated was still enough to display to the world.

sentences.zh: 彼之不死，宜欲得當以報漢也。

translations.literal: That he did not die—he surely wished to obtain an occasion to repay Han.
translations.idiomatic: That he did not die—he surely wished to obtain an occasion to repay Han.

sentences.zh: 」上以遷為誣罔，欲沮貳師，為陵遊說，下遷腐刑。

translations.literal: " The emperor considered Qian's words deceptive and false, thought he wished to discourage the Eshi general and was lobbying for Ling, and sent Qian down to castration punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor considered Qian's words deceptive, thought he wished to discourage the Eshi general and was lobbying for Ling, and imposed castration on Qian.

sentences.zh: 久之，上悔陵無救，曰：「陵當發出塞，乃詔強弩都尉令迎軍；

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor regretted that Ling had no relief, and said: "When Ling should have set out beyond the passes, I then ordered the Strong Crossbow Colonel to meet the army;
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the emperor regretted that Ling had no relief and said, "When Ling should have set out beyond the passes, I had ordered the Strong Crossbow Colonel to meet his army;

sentences.zh: 坐預詔之，得令老將生奸詐。

translations.literal: because I announced it in advance, this allowed the old general to breed deceit.
translations.idiomatic: because I announced it in advance, this allowed the old general to breed deceit.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使勞賜陵餘軍得脫者。

translations.literal: " He thereupon sent envoys to comfort and reward those of Ling's remaining army who had escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon sent envoys to comfort and reward those of Ling's remaining army who had escaped.

sentences.zh: ----3上以法制御下，好尊用酷吏，而郡、國二千石為治者大抵多酷暴，吏民益輕犯法；

translations.literal: ----3 The emperor used law to control subordinates and liked to honor and employ harsh clerks; moreover commandery and state two-thousand-bushel administrators governing were mostly harsh and violent; officials and people increasingly treated violating law lightly;
translations.idiomatic: ----3 The emperor used law to control subordinates and liked to employ harsh clerks; commandery and state two-thousand-bushel administrators were mostly harsh and violent; officials and people increasingly treated breaking the law lightly;

sentences.zh: 東方盜賊滋起，大群至數千人，攻城邑，取庫兵，釋死罪，縛辱郡太守、都尉，殺二千石；

translations.literal: eastern bandits increasingly rose; large bands reached several thousand men, attacked cities and towns, seized arsenal weapons, released death-crime prisoners, bound and insulted commandery governors and commandants, and killed two-thousand-bushel officials;
translations.idiomatic: eastern bandits rose in force; large bands reached thousands, attacked cities and towns, seized arsenal weapons, released condemned men, bound and insulted commandery governors and commandants, and killed two-thousand-bushel officials;

sentences.zh: 小群以百數掠鹵鄉里者，不可勝數，道路不通。

translations.literal: small bands numbering in the hundreds plundering villages were beyond counting; roads were impassable.
translations.idiomatic: small bands of hundreds plundering villages were beyond counting; roads were impassable.

sentences.zh: 上始使御史中丞、丞相長史督之，弗能禁；

translations.literal: The emperor at first sent the Vice Censor-in-Chief and the Chancellor's Chief Clerk to supervise them—they could not stop it;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first sent the Vice Censor-in-Chief and the Chancellor's Chief Clerk to supervise them but could not stop it;

sentences.zh: 乃使光祿大夫范昆及故九卿張德等衣繡衣，持節、虎符，發兵以興擊。

translations.literal: he thereupon sent Palace Counselor Fan Kun and former Nine Ministers Zhang De and others clothed in embroidered robes, holding credentials and tiger tallies, to raise troops and strike them down.
translations.idiomatic: he then sent Palace Counselor Fan Kun and former Nine Ministers Zhang De and others in embroidered robes, holding credentials and tiger tallies, to raise troops and strike them down.

sentences.zh: 斬首大部或至萬餘級，及以法誅通行、飲食當連坐者，諸郡甚者數千人。

translations.literal: Beheaded in major cases sometimes reached more than ten thousand; moreover by law those executed for association in travel and eating and drinking reached several thousand in some commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Major beheadings sometimes reached more than ten thousand; moreover those executed by law for association in travel and dining reached thousands in some commanderies.

sentences.zh: 數歲，乃頗得其渠率，散卒失亡復聚黨阻山川者往往而群居，無可奈何。

translations.literal: Several years later they somewhat obtained their ringleaders; scattered soldiers who lost and fled and again gathered parties blocking mountains and rivers often grouped and dwelt together—nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later they somewhat captured ringleaders; scattered men who fled and again gathered in mountain strongholds often lived in groups—nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 於是作《沈命法》，曰：「群盜起，不發覺，發覺而捕弗滿品者，二千石以下至小吏，主者皆死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made the Shenming Law, saying: "When bandit gangs rise, if not discovered, or discovered but capture does not reach the quota, from two-thousand-bushel officials down to minor clerks, those in charge all die.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he enacted the Shenming Law, saying, "When bandit gangs rise, if not discovered, or discovered but capture does not reach the quota, from two-thousand-bushel officials down to minor clerks, those in charge all die.

sentences.zh: 」其後小吏畏誅，雖有盜不敢發，恐不能得，坐課累府，府亦使其不言。

translations.literal: " Afterward minor clerks feared execution; though there were bandits they dared not report them, fearing they could not obtain the quota and would sit in assessment and burden the prefecture; the prefecture also had them not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward minor clerks feared execution; though there were bandits they dared not report them, fearing they could not meet the quota and would burden the prefecture in assessment; the prefecture also had them keep silent.

sentences.zh: 故盜賊多，上下相為匿，以文辭避法焉。

translations.literal: Therefore bandits were many; superiors and subordinates concealed for one another and used literary phrases to evade the law.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore bandits were many; superiors and subordinates concealed for one another and used literary phrases to evade the law.

sentences.zh: 是時，暴勝之為直指使者，所誅殺二千石以下尤多，威振州郡。

translations.literal: At this time Bao Sheng-zhi was a direct-pointing envoy; those he executed and killed below two-thousand-bushel rank were especially many; his authority shook provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Bao Sheng-zhi was a direct-pointing envoy; those he executed below two-thousand-bushel rank were especially many; his authority shook provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 至勃海，聞郡人雋不疑賢，請與相見。

translations.literal: Reaching Bohai, he heard that the commandery man Jun Buyi was worthy and requested to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Bohai, he heard that the commandery man Jun Buyi was worthy and requested to meet him.

sentences.zh: 不疑容貌尊嚴，衣冠甚偉，勝之躧履起迎，登堂坐定，不疑據地曰：「竊伏海瀕，聞暴公子舊矣，今乃承顏接辭。

translations.literal: Buyi's appearance was dignified and imposing; his cap and robes very grand; Sheng-zhi slipped off his shoes and rose to greet him; ascending the hall and sitting settled, Buyi leaned on the ground and said: "Your servant secretly dwells by the sea's edge and has long heard of Master Bao; now I receive your face and exchange words.
translations.idiomatic: Buyi's appearance was dignified and imposing; his cap and robes very grand; Sheng-zhi slipped off his shoes and rose to greet him; once seated in the hall, Buyi leaned forward and said, "Your servant dwells secretly by the sea and has long heard of Master Bao; now I receive your face and exchange words.

sentences.zh: 凡為吏，太剛則折，太柔則廢，威行，施之以恩，然後樹功揚名，永終天祿。

translations.literal: In general as an official, too rigid then one breaks, too soft then one is discarded; when authority is established, apply kindness upon it—only then establish merit and raise one's name and eternally complete Heaven's stipend.
